key_takeaways: RIL is explicitly trading near-term consumer margins for digital scale (Retail) and building new infrastructure moats (dark stores; data centers; AI/media tooling).

In Energy/O2C, management stresses realizable margin is constrained by procurement/logistics friction even when market cracks are extreme; nonetheless, RIL demonstrated operational resilience (near-full runs) and feedstock advantage (ethane-heavy slate).

Forward commentary is deliberately non-committal on near-term O2C earnings due to geopolitical volatility (“a lot of imponderables”), but management maintains confidence in structural positioning: “structurally… we are in a good place right through.”

quarters.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd anticipates continued growth in its consumer businesses, which now contribute over 55% of EBITDA, despite macroeconomic challenges such as energy price shocks and INR depreciation. The company is focusing on strategic initiatives in AI, retail expansion, and new energy projects to drive future growth.

subsections.label: Consolidated performance highlights (FY26 and Q4)
points: FY26: Revenue +10%, EBITDA +13.5% (includes a one-time gain from sale of listed shares).
Consumer businesses now contribute >55% of EBITDA.
Q4: Consolidated EBITDA flat; consumer (Jio + Retail) +14% offset energy weakness.
PAT declined QoQ due to higher depreciation & interest from 5G asset capitalization.

subsections.label: O2C (Refining, Marketing, Petrochemicals): war-driven dislocation, agility in crude sourcing, and near-term risk factors
points: Strait of Hormuz disruption: estimated ~10 mbpd supply cut; IEA release 400m barrels over 3–4 months (~3.5–4 mbpd offset).

Transit flows down materially; Dubai crude surged to $168; LNG briefly $27/mmbtu; freight up 10–15x; crude premiums reportedly $20–$30/bbl (and instances…$40/bbl); insurance from $25–30k to millions of dollars.

RIL response: lost 40–50% of refinery feed previously tied to Middle East; mitigated via agile sourcing from Venezuela, Russia, Brazil, Mexico; relied on capability of processing more than 200 grades of crude.
Increased domestic support: LPG supplies almost fourfold; increased gas availability to domestic market (linked to E&P/R-cluster gas).

subsections.label: Segmental direction (FY26)
points: Digital: EBITDA +18%, driven by subscribers/5G mix, broadband, engagement.
Retail: EBITDA +8%, muted by hyperlocal e-commerce scale-up and softer fashion/lifestyle demand.
O2C: EBITDA +10% despite geopolitical and feedstock/logistics volatility.
Oil & Gas: pressured by production decline (reservoir reserves coming down).

subsections.label: Jio Platforms / RJIL: scale, margin expansion, and product roadmap
points: Subscribers 524m (net adds 36.3m FY; 9.1m in Q4).
5G users 268m (+77m FY): largest outside of China for a single-country operator.
Fixed broadband 27m (+~10m FY); JioAirFiber homes 12.9m; ~75% of new home connects via AirFiber.
Network usage: 241 Exabytes FY; Q4 66 Exabytes; +31% YoY. Per-capita data consumption 42.3 GB/month; churn reducing.
ARPU ₹214, +4% YoY despite no tariff action (organic drivers).

subsections.label: Strategic/technical initiatives (notable)
points: AI-first network operations: AI automations, energy optimization.
Proprietary RAN innovations: proprietary beam form cell design to boost capacity in high-density venues (stadiums/traffic zones).
Network slicing: already used for fixed wireless; planned monetization via enterprise assured-throughput and potentially B2C use cases like gaming, subject to market, the regulations.
Homes execution at scale: 50 to 60,000 homes in a day, >90% installs within 24 hours, expanding addressable market via non-line-of-sight (NLOS) deployment.

Enterprise momentum: managed connectivity (Wi-Fi/firewall/surveillance), UBR last-mile, dispersed-location AirFiber, larger deal wins, dedicated terabyte-level connectivity, SME compute via JioPC (AI-ready).
IPO: management said it is fairly imminent…work has been done…we will keep you posted in the coming days.

AI data centers: clarified not within Jio Platforms; will sit under the intelligence business at RIL/entity created. Work underway for captive/partner capacity in Jamnagar and targeting gigawatt scale data centers over coming quarters.

subsections.label: Petchem specifics (Amit Chaturvedi)
points: Middle East accounts for 13% ethylene capacity and 25% global commodity chemicals exports; Hormuz blockage stranded ~3.8m tonnes/month naphtha flows plus large polymer exports.
Asia crackers hit by naphtha shortages and LNG disruption (Qatar force majeure referenced); ethylene operating rates in Asia dropped 80% → 60%.

Feedstock economics: naphtha price up (annual avg $726, +13% YoY); ethane down ~14%; naphtha-based ethylene margins severely negative, while ethane-based remained healthy—RIL advantaged as ~75%…from non-naphtha sources.
Demand: PE/PP +3%, PVC -10% (import disruption), fiber +5%, polyester +1% with better PET into summer season.
Government actions: temporary customs duty exemption on key petrochem products through current quarter; likely to be revoked in Q2 if prices moderate.
Priorities: execute large projects—vinyl and PTA—and leverage integration (refinery off-gases, surplus naphtha, stable US ethane virtual ethane pipeline).

subsections.label: International expansion
points: FMCG presence in 40 countries.

subsections.label: E&P: managed decline, CBM growth, and gas price dynamics amid LNG disruption
points: KG-D6 decline managed to ~8% vs expected 12–14%; EBITDA margin slightly lower due to higher opex from integrity refurbishment and labor.
Growth in CBM continues; drilling 40 multilateral wells for productivity.
Pricing: KG-D6 constrained by ceiling price; revised ceiling to ~$8.9/MMBtu; CBM is market-linked (no ceiling).

LNG disruption view: Qatar Ras Laffan damage referenced; management suggested restoration could take almost five years, which could keep prices elevated near-term even as US LNG capacity additions arrive.

subsections.label: Retail (RRVL): growth led by hyperlocal scale; margin mix pressure acknowledged
points: Q4 revenue ₹98,000 cr (highest ever; Q4 exceeded Q3), +11% YoY; ~14% adjusted for RCPL demerger.
Q4 EBITDA ₹6,900 cr; margin 7.9%; PAT ₹3,500 cr.
FY transactions 1.93bn, +39% (management linked higher transaction growth vs revenue growth to high-frequency quick commerce orders).
Network: 333 net new stores in Q4; crossed 20,000 stores; crossed 1,000 big-box hypermarket/supermarket milestone.

subsections.label: Hyperlocal / JioMart operating model
points: Hyperlocal orders: +30% QoQ average daily orders; +300% YoY.
Reach: serving 1,200+ cities via 3,100 stores (dark + walk-in) claimed widest network.

Differentiation: hyperlocal expanded beyond grocery—electronics stores + 1,700+ fashion stores on platform enabling two-hour delivery with entire full store assortment (vs limited dark-store assortments).
3P marketplace expansion to fill assortment gaps; new app version improved conversions and values.

subsections.label: Category notes
points: Grocery & fashion called standout with strong double-digit growth; LFL in mid-to-high single digits.
Fashion: 1,500 stores refreshed; tech enablement (self-checkout, RFID). AI operating model across design-to-fulfillment.
Ajio: steady; industry leading bill values; Ajio Rush 4-hour delivery in 600+ cities.
Shein: strong momentum, scaling to 1,000 new options/day, now investing in brand promotion.
Premium/Luxe: portfolio expansion (e.g., exclusive Kurt Geiger partnership); Ajio Luxe brand portfolio +24% YoY.
Jewels: average bill value +53% YoY, diamond mix rising (margin supportive).
Consumer electronics: first ever ₹500 cr sales in a single day during Digital India sale; ResQ services in 1,600+ locations.

subsections.label: Management stance on competition/consolidation & margins
points: Competitive response: Reliance views stores as omni stores; dark stores only to fill the gaps where network designed for walk-in cannot meet service levels.
No consolidation commitment: too early…let us see how the industry evolves.
Margin dilution: explicitly attributed to mix—hyperlocal growing faster; If we slow down the growth of online business, margin will start improving.

subsections.label: Media & Entertainment (JioStar / JioHotstar / Jio Studios): engagement records and tech-led monetization
points: Platform scale & sports-driven peaks: March MAUs 550m; even without marquee cricket, steady…over 400 million MAUs.
T20 World Cup: world record 72.5m concurrent streams (previous global record 65m); highest ever monetization of the tournament despite earlier RMG ad ban.
IPL momentum: opening weekend largest ever; reach +15%, connected TV reach +27% (as of CSK-MI match).

subsections.label: Product/tech launches (notable)
points: Tadka micro-content: over 100 shows, vertical + horizontal content.
ChatGPT integration for voice search and Indian-language/accent recognition.
In-app commerce: Swiggy integration enabling ordering during live matches without ever leaving.

subsections.label: Entertainment / TV economics
points: Linear TV share 34.7%, almost in line with next three networks combined.
Digital entertainment watch time +35%; record digital entertainment ad revenue growth (broader client base).
TV entertainment ad revenue under pressure due to FMCG spend cuts, but careful cost management delivered industry leading annual EBITDA margins.
On profitability question: management emphasized profitability is a portfolio outcome; we have a very large and profitable entertainment business…driven a lot by TV.

subsections.label: Jio Studios
points: Highlighted Dhurandhar as a ₹1000 crores plus franchise per film, crossing 40% of India’s overall box office, and highest-grossing Indian film overseas; large music-platform performance (40 billion plus views).
Claimed Jio Studios is largest Indian content studio by revenue/catalog/box office share; 500+ awards.

subsections.label: FMCG (RCPL / consumer products): rapid scale, manufacturing buildout, and M&A
points: FY revenue ₹22,000 cr; Q4 ₹7,350 cr—both stated as ~2x YoY.
Campa revenue ₹4,700 cr, now fourth largest carbonated soft drink brand.
Independence essentials revenue ₹2,600 cr; packaged water now third largest water player.
International expansion: presence in 40 countries.
Distribution scale: 5,000+ distributors and ~3m outlets.
Capex/industrialization: targeting leadership in cooldrinks manufacturing; ~12 plants and more planned; developing integrated food parks for multi-category output/cost efficiency.
M&A: acquired Goodness Group (Australia; functional/health beverages) and 100% stake in Manna (Tamil Nadu; millet-based products).
Clarified in Q&A that brand numbers cited were partial: beverages category >₹6,000 cr; daily essentials ~40% of revenue.

subsections.label: Macro context & what changed in March (management framing)
points: Management described FY26 as a tale of two periods: the first 11 months saw robust domestic activity, steady energy prices, and strong 5G traffic; March saw an acute energy shock with prices almost doubling, 70% higher in some cases, and gas up to double.

subsections.label: Key macro headwinds flagged
points: Supply shock from the war and its impact on industry and consumer confidence.
INR depreciation: 11% for the year and 4% just in March, with downside bias if disruption persists.

Management expects home additions to ramp further, not peak.
Aim to begin RERTC revenue/EBITDA contribution next year.

Oil demand growth muted (~0.7 mbpd) due to tariff concerns.
PVC and PET softer due to heavy rains/floods and weak summer.

key_takeaways: Resilience under stress: O2C performance framed as operationally strong despite extreme, quantifiable cost shocks (freight/premiums/insurance) and crude availability constraints.
Structural pivot visible in EBITDA mix: consumer businesses now >55% of EBITDA, and Q4 showed consumer growth offsetting energy volatility.

Jio margin expansion without tariff: continued EBITDA margin improvement (RJIL 56.2%) tied to scale, AI/network efficiency, and product upsell—while keeping optionality for premium/sliced services pending regulatory readiness.

Retail growth increasingly mix-driven: hyperlocal scaling is driving transactions and reach but pressuring EBITDA margin; management explicitly treats it as a deliberate trade-off dependent on channel mix.

New Energy commercial traction: signed one of the world’s largest green ammonia supply contract with Samsung C&T; execution across Kutch generation, Jamnagar chemicals, and gigafactories remains the near-term proof point.
JioStar productization: meaningful push into AI-enabled UX (ChatGPT search) and commerce integration (Swiggy) suggests monetization expansion beyond ads/subscription into transaction-led use cases.

quarters.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd continues to demonstrate strong growth across its diversified business segments, with significant investments in new energy and digital services, while maintaining a steady balance sheet and cash flow.

Cash generation exceeds capex: Capex run-rate remains elevated (~₹34,000 cr in Q3), but management emphasized 'we continue to generate more cash.' Net debt and leverage described as 'fairly steady' with 'no change' in key balance sheet metrics.

subsections.label: Jio Platforms (Digital Services)
points: Network-led scale, home broadband acceleration, enterprise upsell.
Subscriber engine remains strong: Total subscribers 515.3m, net adds 8.9m in Q3.
5G subs 253m+; Jio claims '65% share of 5G subscribers in India.'
53% of Jio traffic now on 5G, easing 4G congestion and improving UX; management cited Ookla recognition as best network.
Jio highlighted dominance in incremental activity: 'caught into 99% of incremental industry VLR subscriber additions' over 12 months to Nov 2025.
ARPU expansion is organic; no hike planned: ARPU ₹213.7, up sequentially; management: 'There is no impact of tariff increase… completely driven by organic means.'
On future hikes: 'no comments… no such plans', targeting 'organically… improve our ARPU by 5% to 6% a year.'
Homes / fixed broadband is scaling rapidly, increasingly via wireless last-mile: 25m+ fixed broadband connections, adding ~1m+ homes per month for 7 straight months.
JioAirFiber 11.5m homes (5G FWA).
Jio claims 50%+ share of broadband subs nationally; '70% of incremental fixed broadband subscriber addition is happening through the Jio network.'
Strategic shift: last-mile increasingly wireless; management argued FWA quality 'at par, if not better, than fiber' and FWA subscribers consume more data.

Operational enablement: creation of '3D Twins for every network tower… every building' to automate best-technology selection at premise level; 'no manual intervention' needed for provisioning decisions.

Capacity management: Jio is 'optimizing… the number of customers… on the 5G FWA' to avoid local constraints; expects most new adds to come via UBR / point-to-point spectrum-based FWA where 'there is no capacity constraint most of the times.'

Enterprise monetization vector expanding (no revenue split disclosed): Focus on Managed Services, managed Wi‑Fi, regulated sovereign cloud, and DC-to-DC high throughput/low latency connectivity for AI-era requirements.
Enterprise line is 'growing much faster than the rest of the revenue line items', but management will provide split later.

Cloud stack positioning: core cloud is a Jio service (incl. MeghRaj/sovereign), while AI products will be developed by Reliance Intelligence and offered via Jio. Capex for data centers/GPUs sits with RIL or Reliance Intelligence, while Jio remains asset-light, accessing infra via leases.
Partnership-driven bundling now generates revenue (not cost): Google Gemini Pro offer: 'available for all of our unlimited 5G users' with 18-month subscription (MRP value claim ₹35,000).
Critically, Jio claims 'there is no cost to Jio… these are now revenue generating opportunities for Jio', and confirmed that for such offers partners pay Jio ('That is right.').

subsections.label: Reliance Retail
points: Growth masked by accounting/seasonality; quick commerce scaling with positive contribution margin.
Quarter performance and distortions: Revenue ₹97,600 cr (+8.1%), highest ever quarter.

Key offsets to headline growth: (1) GST rate rationalization (effective Sep 22), (2) festival season split between Q2 and Q3 (vs last year concentrated in Q3), (3) RCPL demerger effective Dec 1 (RCPL revenue included fully in Q2, partially removed in Q3 and fully absent from Q4 retail numbers).
Management insisted underlying growth is stronger: 'adjusted… it is a decent double-digit growth'; and on Q2+Q3 combined: 'decent 13%, 14% revenue growth.'
Margins: EBITDA ₹6,915 cr, margin 8%.

Margin headwinds this quarter: festive promotions, hyperlocal/quick commerce investments, and one-time new labour code impact (gratuity etc.). CFO later characterized labor code impact as 'not material' at an aggregate level.
Demerger impact on EBITDA to be clearer next quarter; retail CFO: 'We will have to wait for the next quarter.'
Quick commerce / hyperlocal: now a scale business inside retail.
Orders at 1.6m run-rate (Dec); +53% QoQ and +360% YoY.
Positioning: 'on track to be the second largest QC player' (Group CFO) and claims largest reach: 5,000+ pin codes in 1,000+ cities supported by 3,000+ stores (walk-in + dark stores).
Dark stores: ~800; <30% of the 3,000-store QC fulfillment network.

Unit economics claim (important): 'on a contribution margin level, we are positive.' Management attributes this to: Strong procurement economics: 'one of the largest vendors… pretty efficient sourcing.'
High-margin fresh & vegetables + low wastage: typical market wastage '30–35%'; Reliance cites supply chain strength.
High F&V mix drives repeat: 'Almost 1 in 3 to 1 in 4 orders… have F&V', leading to ~2x higher transaction intensity vs other platforms (claim).

Margin outlook for QC inside retail: delivery adds variable cost, but leveraging existing store infrastructure should keep it accretive; CFO emphasized wallet share and said QC is 'margin positive… adding rupee margin… accretive for me.'
Category highlights: Grocery: big-box + staples/packaged foods momentum; gifting categories at 'highest ever volumes.'
Metro B2B: growth driven by footfalls; focus shifting to wallet share via loyalty/engagement.
Fashion: weaker YoY in Q3 due to demand pull-forward into Q2; omnichannel reach allows 30-min/2-hr/same-day/next-day delivery in 1,300+ cities.
Ajio: AOV +21% YoY, 2.8m live options, Ajio Rush live in 420 pin codes / 10 cities, next-day delivery to 26 cities; faster delivery reduces returns.
Shein: scaling; 6.5m+ app installs, 50,000+ options.
Jewellery: growth largely price-led; bill values +73%; Dhanteras LFL +21%; old-gold exchange share 21%→29%.
Digital electronics: strong festive quarter aided by GST resets (ACs/TVs); resQ service network in 1,600+ cities enables fast install (competitive advantage).
Store footprint / consolidation: Consolidation largely complete; churn will remain '2%, 3% of your portfolio' via relocations, but management expects net area additions QoQ going forward.

subsections.label: FMCG (Reliance Consumer Products / RCPL)
points: Post-demerger growth, brand acquisitions, capacity build-out.
Structural change: RCPL became direct RIL subsidiary from Dec 1, 2025 (demerger completed).
Scale and growth: Q3 revenue ₹5,000 cr; YTD ₹15,000 cr.
Daily essentials up 1.5x YoY.
Management: now four brands >₹1,000 cr each; Independence brand >₹1,500 cr.
Beverages: 'double-digit shares in key markets'; energy portfolio reached ₹1,000 cr 'for the year' (as stated).
Capacity and footprint expansion: 'More than doubling our capacity on beverages this year' with high-speed lines across 12 states.
Food parks: land allocated across multiple states; work begins this/next quarter; one beverage plant at Kurnool ready by March.
M&A / portfolio building (newsworthy): Majority acquisition of Udhaiyam (staples; strong TN distribution) to expand pan-India staples and enter pulses meaningfully.
Acquired global brands (except some territories): Brylcreem, Toni & Guy, Badedas, Matey (UK children’s personal care).
Category entries/launches: pet food (pilots in southern cities), relaunch SIL, entry into noodles (4-city launch, expand next quarter).

subsections.label: Media & Entertainment (JioStar / JioHotstar)
points: Platform stickiness beyond cricket; ad market still pressured on TV.

Platform operating metrics: MAUs 450m, +13% QoQ; notable because Q3 had 'very little cricket'—management stressed conversion from sports-led acquisition to entertainment-led retention: 'convert… from cricket to entertainment and keep them… sticky.'
Entertainment watch time +15% QoQ, with record digital entertainment monetization, driven by CTV mix and stronger content monetization.
Content performance: Bigg Boss franchise across Hindi + 4 southern markets drove '40% growth on digital watch time' and 'highest ever ad revenues' for the property.
AI content: Mahabharat claimed as 'one of our best launches' with '2x viewership growth over any of our best performing shows.'
Sports performance: Women’s World Cup: live watch time 10x vs prior edition; viewers 4x; peak concurrency 21m; final match viewership 'in par with men’s cricket… as good as any IPL match.'
Pro Kabaddi: watch time +120% YoY, reinforcing #2 sport after cricket.
Men’s bilaterals: watch time and viewers ~55% above pre-merger levels.
Linear TV: Network share 34.6% (+100 bps), equal to 'next three networks all put together.'
TV ad market remains challenging due to FMCG and consumer electronics spend cuts, but December shows recovery post-GST.
Financials: Operating revenue ₹6,896 cr, EBITDA ₹1,303 cr; management cautioned YoY comparability given merger only began Nov 14 in prior period.

subsections.label: Upstream (E&P)
points: Decline management, infill/extension plans, CBM productivity improving.
Core focus: 'manage the decline' in KG-D6; actual decline running ~12% lower than FDP plan (management claim).
Quarter output / economics: LNG-linked prices softened: $11 → $9.5; KG-D6 subject to ceiling price; CBM market-linked.
EBITDA ~₹4,850 cr, pressured by lower volume and price.
RIL remains significant supplier: India produces 90–95 MMSCMD, KG-D6+CBM contribute ~26.5 MMSCMD.
Oil/condensate steady: ~17.3 kbpd avg.
CBM is improving materially: early campaign productivity up 2–2.5x; recent campaign '3.5 to 4 times' (vs earlier wells), with better results even outside core areas.
Forward plan: Rig mobilization in 2H of the year.
KG basin exploration via infrastructure-led exploration (tiebacks).
KG-D6: workovers in MJ + additional wells in R cluster and SAT cluster.
CBM: continue multilateral wells.

Market view: LNG supply rising (US exports +30 mt cited); China demand 'tepid' but potential rebound; key price triggers: weather + China rebound. India demand growth driven by CGD; PNGRB uniform tariff policy (zones 3→2) seen as supportive.

subsections.label: O2C (Refining, Marketing, Petrochemicals)
points: Strong fuel cracks offset by feed/freight; petrochem resilient via ethane advantage and domestic focus.
Refining & Marketing: EBITDA ₹16,507 cr (+15% YoY), supported by strong transportation fuels.
Fuel cracks up ~60%–100% YoY (diesel ~60%, gasoline ~100% cited).
Domestic placement emphasized; via Jio-bp: diesel sales +25%, gasoline +21%; combined gasoline+diesel volumes +24%.
CBG/CNG volumes +55% to 10,000 tonnes (as stated).
Headwinds managed: Feedstock cost pressure from higher Middle East OSPs and higher freight (VLCC availability reduced due to sanctions).
Mitigations: record gasifier output reducing external fuel needs; fuel mix optimization; grid power sourcing; higher time-charter share; cargo aggregation; tanker service flexibility.
Product mix optimization: maximized gasoline vs routing to petrochem (better economics).

Jio-bp network expansion: outlets 2,125, charge points 6,815, CBG/CNG stations 121, convenience stores 164; market effectiveness: gasoline 1.8x and diesel 2.7x sales per outlet vs competition (company-defined metric).
Macro/industry frame: Brent down 15% amid oversupply; margins supported by high global refinery operating rates and disruptions; China stock build 400–500 kbd cited as supporting crude.

Petrochemicals: Ethane-based advantage is central to resilience: Management showed multi-year economics where naphtha cracking margins collapsed; stated: 'roughly three-fourth of our portfolio is based on… [ethane/ROGC]… and about one-fourth is naphtha based.'
Feedstock and margin environment: Ethane prices +21% YoY (winter Henry Hub $3.56 vs $2.2 last year).
Naphtha -14% YoY (crude weakness).
Polymer deltas: PE delta +6%, PP delta -12%, PVC delta -5%; polyester weak (MEG), partially offset by PX strength.
Execution levers emphasized: Domestic market focus for higher netbacks.
Tight inventory discipline: operating with '8 to 10 days of inventory' to minimize stock-loss risk amid volatility.
Demand commentary (India): PE demand +4%, PP +8%.
PVC demand -12% due to prolonged monsoon (agri/infrastructure linkage), but RIL placed all volumes domestically due to structural deficit.
Polyester: PSF +5%, filament -1% (imports; addressed via MIP), PET -15% (weather-linked demand).

Industry restructuring as a medium-term tailwind: Capacity rationalization cited: Korea targeting 3.5 mt ethylene shutdown; Exxon shutting Singapore cracker; closures in Europe; China 'anti-involution policy' to shut older plants.
Management expects restoration of balance 'might take about a year or so.'
Projects: execution focus on Vinyl and PTA projects; continued expansion of domestic downstream solutions and Jio-bp footprint.

subsections.label: New Energy: integrated solar + battery + generation ecosystem commissioning; strategic emphasis on supply chain sovereignty
points: Strategic framing: In current geopolitics/tariffs/supply chain disruptions, RIL argues its integrated chain provides five advantages: value chain margin control, scale, customer solutions, business model flexibility, and 'supply chain security and sufficiency.'
Manufacturing status (Jamnagar) – concrete commissioning updates: Solar module manufacturing commissioned; yields '94%–95%.'
Solar cell (HJT) commissioned and ramping.
Ingot & wafer pilot commissioned; scaling to giga-scale with commissioning in 'next few quarters,' ramp to 10 GW during the year.
Polysilicon and solar glass: construction advanced; both targeted for commissioning during the year; described as among the largest outside China.
Expansion-ready: utilities/infrastructure built for 20 GW, not only 10 GW.
Battery gigafactory: Phase 1: 40 GWh, with expansion to 100 GWh (modular).
Equipment already on site; construction 'full swing'; commissioning in phases during the year.
Generation at Kutch (550,000 acres): Targeting 125–150 GWp solar; management cited '300 billion units' on an RTC basis (also acknowledged as increased from earlier plans).
Near-term: generation capacity starts coming up in 'next 12 to 15 months.'

Use case hierarchy: largely captive (refinery, new energy complex, data centers) and conversion into green fuels for domestic and export markets (Japan/Korea/Europe mentioned as off-take interest areas).

Cost competitiveness vs China: RIL acknowledged China benchmark but argued integrated chain and especially power cost advantage via RTC green power is key: 'single most variable… is the power cost' (polysilicon), and integrated RTC power provides 'additional leverage.'

Supply risk (silver export restrictions): Management not concerned: HJT uses lower silver than TOPCon/IBC; multiple initiatives to reduce silver; consumption is 'milligrams per watt… kgs per gigawatt.'

subsections.label: Material credit milestone
points: S&P upgraded RIL from BBB+ to A- (two notches), citing a higher share of earnings from 'less cyclical businesses, especially the consumer side' and expectation that earnings growth will outpace capex via free cash flow.
CFO called it: 'first Indian manufacturing company with an international rating of A-.'

subsections.label: Funding flexibility for power generation assets
points: On New Energy generation capex, CFO reiterated optionality: generation assets 'need not be… entirely on our balance sheet', suggesting potential structuring akin to utility assets while maintaining rating discipline.

guidance_ledger.statement: Targeting organically improve our ARPU by 5% to 6% a year.
Management expects home additions to ramp further, not peak.
Aim to begin RERTC revenue/EBITDA contribution next year.

quarters.summary: Infosys lowered FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1.5%-3% YoY in constant currency (from 1.5%-3.5% previously) after a soft Q1 (2.4% YoY, 1% QoQ CC) impacted by a one-time client program termination, softer volumes and pricing, and a European manufacturing client de-scoping; operating margin guidance was maintained at 20%-22%. Management flagged an uncertain macro environment, continued strong AI revenue momentum (8.2% of revenue, growing double-digit QoQ), robust large deal wins ($3.6bn TCV, 61% net new), and announced CEO succession with Ashiss Dash to take over from Salil Parekh on April 1, 2027.

subsections.label: Revenue drivers
points: Q1 revenue growth was lower than expectations mainly due to a one-off 50 bps impact from program termination by an EURS client during the quarter, not factored into earlier guidance.
Volumes were soft and weaker than expectations and versus historical Q1 trends.
Client expectation on productivity along with high competitive intensity resulted in softer price increases versus expectations.
Sequential revenue growth was also impacted by higher offshoring to derisk the business model, along with lower revenues from a European Manufacturing client called out in the last earnings call.

subsections.label: Margin bridge
points: Despite lower-than-expected growth, gross margins improved 60 bps sequentially and operating margin improved 20 bps sequentially to 21.1%.
Tailwinds: 70 bps from rupee depreciation, 20 bps from Project Maximus, and a 10 bps net benefit from amortization of costs on intangibles incurred in Q4, offset by impact of new acquisitions in Q1.
Headwinds: 50 bps from investment in AI sales and marketing, 40 bps from one-time revenue impact from program termination.
A one-time cost benefit of ~30 bps was offset by 20 bps due to increase in various other expenses.

Every 1% change/depreciation in rupee vs dollar typically gives 15-17 bps margin benefit, but since dollar appreciation is often broad-based against many currencies (Infosys has ~45% revenue from non-US geography), part of the rupee depreciation benefit gets offset.
Company will face a headwind from compensation increases in the second half of the year but remains confident of holding the 20%-22% guidance band.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & cash
points: Balance sheet continues to be strong and debt-free.
Cash returned to shareholders through dividends exceeded $1 bn during the quarter.

subsections.label: Compensation
points: Compensation increases will be rolled out in two parts: October 2026 and January 2027.
Most employees will get an increase in October; senior employees will get it in January.

subsections.label: Deal traction and pipeline
points: Large deal pipeline is even larger than the current 8% AI revenue share, indicating good traction ahead.
5 of the large deals were consolidation deals where Infosys was the beneficiary; 3 deals were just under the $500mn mega deal range.
TCV conversion: consolidation deals convert to revenue quicker; transformation deals ramp up more slowly - this dynamic has not changed materially over recent quarters.
AI is now integral to almost every client discussion and deal, including Topaz Fabric; it is not tracked as separate AI-specific TCV since it underlies virtually all engagements.

Renewals on large deals traditionally see productivity asks from clients; on top of this, AI-led deflation is now an additional headwind, both on large deal and non-large deal portions of the book, partly offset by net new business won.

subsections.label: Lost renewals / deal discipline
points: Infosys lost some existing renewals; management declined to comment on specific deals but stated the focus is on working with clients on projects/contracts that make economic sense.
Decision to not bid beyond a certain point on a large European client deal was made because it did not make commercial/economic sense, impacting Q4 as the deal reaches closure in December.

subsections.label: Outcome-based pricing
points: Clients show stronger interest in outcome-based pricing, though it is not yet a large part of overall activity; more relevant in heavy transformation investment scenarios.
Outcome-based pricing is a specific track within Project Maximus with a dedicated organizational leader working across all segments to drive it.

subsections.label: Financial Services
points: Growth expected to be higher than company average going forward.
Uncertainty and geopolitical instability causing client hesitancy; spending patterns more cautious.
Client priorities centered on efficiency, productivity, and modernization with discretionary spend evaluated more carefully.
Momentum seen across banking, payments, capital markets, and wealth management.

AI adoption has been incremental and additive, with clients engaging Infosys to support AI journeys across strategy, platforms, engineering, and operations - reflected in ~$1bn large deal net new TCV this quarter.
GCCs continue to expand; Infosys partnering with clients in setup and growth of GCCs.

subsections.label: EURS (Energy, Utilities, Resources, Services)
points: Segment was impacted by one-off client termination; adjusted for this, growth was strong.
Expected to grow higher than company average for the rest of the year.
Macroeconomic uncertainty continues to influence client spending patterns and decision-making timelines.
Clients driving priorities including cost optimization, operational resilience, productivity improvements and regulatory compliance.
Generative AI emerging as a strong growth catalyst driving process re-imagination and productivity initiatives.
Partnerships with hyperscalers and AI-native companies allowing faster experimentation and ideation.

subsections.label: Manufacturing
points: Growth continues to be impacted due to lower revenue from a large client (previously flagged European Manufacturing client).
Despite the headwind, Manufacturing grew close to/slightly over 1.5% (editor's comment: CC growth 1%), described as commendable given the sector headwind.
Clients remain cautious on discretionary spend; decision-making elongated, especially in European auto.
Impact of tariffs, geopolitical uncertainty, and energy cost keeping budgets tightly controlled.
AI adoption creating new opportunity areas but also raising productivity expectations from clients; better pricing being achieved on AI skills and consulting.
Focus on supporting clients through digital, AI modernization, and consolidation initiatives while balancing growth with disciplined deal selection and sustainable pricing.

subsections.label: Retail and CPG
points: Segment continues to see challenges; still constrained growth, not yet seeing pickup.
Consumer spend remains muted; budgets tightly controlled due to geopolitics, inflation, and tariffs.
Spend shifting towards AI modernization and productivity-led programs funded through operational efficiency and cost optimization.
Clients asking for AI-led productivity commitments leading to new pricing structures.
Infosys leveraging native knowledge of client business processes/technology landscapes augmented with AI.
Large deal pipeline healthy, but decision cycles are longer.

subsections.label: Communications
points: Segment continues to see challenges alongside Retail.
Operating environment remains challenging; clients exercising discipline on discretionary spending, closely scrutinizing investment decisions.
AI reshaping spending patterns; enterprises increasingly prioritizing initiatives with near-term gains.
Telecom undergoing significant transformation with consolidation and M&A, with increased investments especially for OEMs.

subsections.label: Life Sciences
points: Segment will see benefit from the acquisition in Healthcare and Life Sciences.

subsections.label: GCC (Global Capability Centre) portfolio
points: Infosys launched an AI GCC concept; held a client event with leading GCC leadership teams at its Bangalore campus sharing latest AI GCC developments.
Traction on GCC looking very strong; revenue growth and work with GCCs is good, though specific milestones not externally shared.

GCC business has a lifecycle - some GCCs expanding well, others have exited in the past with Infosys sometimes participating in the transition; both GCC-internal work and Infosys's work with GCCs are growing well.

key_figures.label: Employees working on coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)
Addressable market from Hexagon AI strategy (6 value pools)

subsections.label: Hexagon AI Strategy - 6 value pools
points: Six areas of new growth identified: process AI, agents for processes, data/data layer for AI, modernization, AI engineering strategy, and coding tools.
Strong traction across all 6 value pools with higher share of revenues coming from process AI, AI strategy and engineering, and Data for AI.

AI revenue is defined as revenue coming from this strategic framework (Hexagon) described at Investor Day - distinct from internally tracked 'AI infused/augmented' revenue which is not included in the externally reported 8.2% figure.

subsections.label: Topaz Fabric platform
points: Platform enables clients to get benefits of AI while keeping sovereignty of their own data and company knowledge within their organization.
Clients can work with any foundation model - closed, open-weight, or on their own cloud/server.
Provides a harness enabling clients to more fully deploy foundation model benefits into their organization and optimize token cost by matching appropriate models to appropriate tasks.
Not held by Infosys or by the foundation model company - data stays with the client, seen as a major differentiator that may become increasingly important over time.
Almost every client discussion today involves some element of AI and Topaz Fabric since it is now foundational/integral to the work being done.

subsections.label: Frontier Engineers
points: Building a team of Frontier Engineers to support client work; objective set at 6,000 over the next few years.
Capability combines engineering plus business context - an area where Infosys was strong even before the AI wave began.
Plan in place for some time to scale this up, leveraging existing internal capability doing similar work.

subsections.label: Small language models
points: Small language model for banking based on Finacle product set is getting good traction, offering an easy way for clients to leverage a smaller, cheaper, more token-efficient model.
Similar traction seen for IT-Ops small language models; both are part of scaling AI offerings.
No separate margin quantification given for AI deals, but management stated it is comfortable with margins seen in this area.

subsections.label: Cybersecurity and AI safety
points: Approach to cyber security includes work done previously around model security protocols (referenced discussion with 'Mythos' and prior model OPUS 4.7), building understanding of vulnerabilities and how to protect against them for clients.
Each client environment requires its own cyber defense; Infosys supports clients via security operation centers beyond just foundation model work.
Own internal Infosys cyber approach incorporates the same principles.

subsections.label: Innovation fund / AI investments
points: Infosys has an innovation fund investing minority stakes in early-stage companies to explore whether new technology can be deployed across the client base or leveraged in some way.

Several past investments made, historically much in data and analytics, now spanning many other technologies; will look at further opportunities including potentially in Indian AI firms, without confirming any specific plan.

subsections.label: Currency exposure
points: Approximately 45% of revenue comes from non-U.S. geography, which offsets part of the rupee depreciation margin benefit since dollar appreciation is typically broad-based against most currencies, not just the rupee.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning on AI
points: Management views large tech/AI companies (e.g., Microsoft's frontier company, Anthropic/Claude) entering the services space as a positive validation of the services opportunity, not a threat, given Infosys's scale of 300,000+ people and ~1,800 clients versus newer entrants' smaller scale.

Differentiators cited: clear AI strategy with 6 focus areas, investment in AI capability, 80,000 employees actively using AI tools for client work, Topaz Fabric enabling data sovereignty and lower token cost, and depth/quality of delivery seen as difficult for competitors to match.
Competition is seen mainly from a few companies given Infosys's client base; differentiation is on AI capability plus depth/quality of delivery.

subsections.label: Productivity and revenue per employee
points: Over the past several quarters (excluding the most recent quarter specifically), the company has seen continuous improvement in revenue productivity.
Productivity benefits are expected to continue even as the company keeps hiring (20,000 planned college graduates this year); pricing dynamics in the market sometimes balance out productivity gains.

subsections.label: CEO succession
points: Salil Parekh's term as CEO ends March 31, 2027; the Board has appointed Ashiss Dash as successor CEO, effective April 1, 2027.

Ashiss Dash has 31 years of experience at Infosys, having worked across delivery, sales, account management, and setting up a new DC in Bhubaneswar; he joined as a software engineer from IIT Kharagpur and has been Segment Head for EURS practice (with many sub-verticals) for many years.

Dash is based in L.A. and will move back to India; over the next 2-3 months he will undergo CEO coaching, then work as Salil's mentee (described elsewhere as 6 months) to prepare for managing a complex $20bn company during a transformational time.
Under Salil's ~10 year tenure, Infosys grew from $10bn to $20bn in revenue, completed digital-era transformation, and launched the AI differentiation/strategy.

Mandate for new CEO: continue executing the existing well-defined AI strategy (Hexagon 6 areas); some fine-tuning expected as a natural evolution, particularly around token cost management and ensuring client data sovereignty, but overall strategy remains unchanged.

subsections.label: Acquisitions
points: Infosys continues to look at acquisitions and has a good pipeline; recently completed acquisitions include Life Sciences/Healthcare (Optimum Healthcare) and Insurance-related (Stratus).

Areas of interest for further M&A include certain geographies for expansion, and industries such as Telco, Financial Services, and a bit more in Healthcare; also areas that are more service-line oriented, especially where AI can be leveraged into processes and agent building.

Company reviewed and decided, after discussion with management team and Board, not to enter the AI infrastructure/data center business at this stage (an area some peers like HCL and TCS have entered).

subsections.label: Project Maximus
points: Project Maximus continues to deliver value from pricing, utilization, and other levers, contributing to margin tailwinds (20 bps in Q1).
Outcome-based pricing is a specific track within Project Maximus, with a dedicated organizational leader driving it across all segments.

subsections.label: Macro uncertainty
points: Overall business environment continues to remain volatile; macro environment remains uncertain.
The lower end of the revised guidance assumes further deterioration in macro; the top end assumes an improvement in macro, though a lesser improvement than assumed in the April guidance.
Clients continue to prioritize investments in AI, modernization, cloud, and productivity initiatives while remaining selective in discretionary spending.

subsections.label: Pricing and competitive intensity
points: Client expectation on productivity, along with high competitive intensity, is resulting in softer-than-expected price increases versus company expectations.
AI-led deflation is an additional headwind on both large deal and non-large deal portions of the book, on top of the traditional productivity ask clients make at contract renewal.

Company does not externally quantify the compression/deflation, though it acknowledges and internally tracks it; in many cases, compression is offset by new/adjacent scope of work with the same client.

subsections.label: Client-specific headwinds
points: One-off 50 bps impact from a program termination by an EURS client during the quarter, not factored into earlier guidance; this was a contract termination for various client reasons, unrelated to AI.

European Manufacturing client: reduced client spend along with Infosys's conscious decision not to pursue certain deals not aligned to return expectations; this impact is now clearly above the previously flagged 0.75%-1% range as the company progressed on certain other deals; will have an additional impact in Q4 as the deal reaches closure in December.

Manufacturing segment growth continues to be impacted by lower revenue from this large client; tariffs, geopolitical uncertainty and energy costs keeping Manufacturing/European auto budgets tightly controlled with elongated decision-making.

subsections.label: Cybersecurity
points: Rising security incidents around autonomous AI agents and breaches at model hosting platforms (referenced OpenAI hack) raise concerns about safety and security of cross-domain AI agent access to client data.
Large corporations are cautious about being locked into a single AI ecosystem given cybersecurity and data-control concerns.

subsections.label: Onsite mix reduction
points: Conscious decision to increase offshoring to derisk the business model is reducing onsite mix, expected to reduce by 0.75% to 1% for the year (excluding new acquisitions), representing an additional headwind versus last year.

key_figures.label: Margin impact from Optimum Healthcare/Stratus acquisitions

subsections.label: Guidance construction
points: Revenue guidance revised down from 1.5%-3.5% CC YoY to 1.5%-3% CC YoY, reflecting Q1 outcome (one-time client program termination), macro factors, volumes, and pricing mix.
As the year progresses, the guidance band is typically narrowed - from a 2-point band to roughly a 1.5-point band by this stage.

Guidance includes ~1.7% contribution from recently closed acquisitions (Optimum Healthcare and Stratus), slightly over 1% impact from the European Manufacturing client (reduced spend plus conscious decision not to pursue certain deals not aligned to return expectations), and ~0.75%-1% impact from shift toward offshore.
Lower end of guidance assumes further macro deterioration; upper end assumes a macro improvement, though less than assumed in the April guidance.
FS and EURS segments are expected to grow higher than the company average for the rest of the year.
Whatever happens in Q1 tends to have a cascading effect across the rest of the fiscal year on guidance.

subsections.label: Margin guidance construction
points: Margin guidance of 20%-22% maintained, assuming headwinds from wage hikes, productivity pass-throughs, AI investments, and a 50 bps impact from the Optimum Healthcare and Stratus acquisitions.
These headwinds are expected to be partly offset by initiatives under Project Maximus and currency benefits.
Company expressed confidence in holding the margin guidance band despite upcoming compensation increase headwinds in H2.

subsections.label: Business outlook
points: Underlying fundamentals of the business remain strong; healthy client engagements leading to a robust pipeline.
Company is taking decisive actions to capitalize on opportunities across the 6 identified AI value pools.
Spending is shifting towards areas with clear business cases such as AI-led Modernization, Cost Transformation, Cybersecurity, Cloud Optimization and Vendor Consolidation.
Normal seasonality expected between first half and second half; nothing unusual anticipated.

guidance_ledger.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised to 1.5% to 3% Y-on-Y growth in constant currency terms (from 1.5%-3.5% previously).
Operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22%.
Effective tax rate expected to be in the range of 29% to 30%.
Onsite mix excluding new acquisitions expected to reduce by 0.75% to 1% for the year.

Guidance includes approximately 1.7% contribution from recently closed acquisitions of Optimum Healthcare and Stratus.
Margin guidance assumes a 50 basis point impact from acquisitions of Optimum Healthcare and Stratus.
Plan to have 6,000 Frontier Engineers over the next few years.
Plan to recruit 20,000 college graduates this year (~4,000 already recruited in Q1).

One-off 50 bps revenue impact from a client terminating a program in the EURS vertical during the quarter; contract termination unrelated to AI.

Reduced client spend plus Infosys's decision not to pursue certain deals not aligned to return expectations; impact now above the previously flagged 0.75%-1% range, with an additional impact expected in Q4 as the deal reaches closure in December.

themes.label: AI-driven transformation
themes.note: AI revenue at 8.2% of overall revenue, growing double-digit QoQ over several quarters, with strong traction across all 6 Hexagon value pools and a $300bn addressable market.

themes.label: Large deal momentum
themes.note: $3.6bn TCV with 61% net new, 22 deals won, 20% from vendor consolidation deals, reflecting continued positive traction in the pipeline.

themes.label: Revenue growth guidance
themes.note: FY27 revenue growth guidance lowered to 1.5%-3% CC YoY from 1.5%-3.5%, driven by Q1 program termination, soft volumes/pricing, and European client impact.

themes.label: Execution risk
themes.note: Client program termination, softer pricing/volumes, and a European Manufacturing client de-scoping created cascading headwinds into the rest of the year.

themes.label: Partnerships and acquisitions
themes.note: Continued pipeline of acquisitions (Optimum Healthcare, Stratus) contributing ~1.7% to revenue guidance; company reviewed but decided against entering AI data center/infrastructure business.

themes.label: Pricing and AI-led deflation

themes.label: Leadership transition

key_takeaways: Our revenue growth for Q1 was at 2.4% Y-on-Y and 1% Q-on-Q in constant currency terms. We had a one-time revenue impact of a client decision during the quarter.
Our AI services revenue was 8.2% of overall revenue in Q1.
Our large deals, $3.6 bn at 61% net new, operating margin at 21.1%, free cash flow at $955 mn. Earnings per share were up 15% Y-on-Y in rupee terms.
We are changing our revenue growth guidance to 1.5% to 3% Y-on-Y growth in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains the same at 20% to 22% operating margin.
The Board has appointed his successor, our new CEO, who will take over on April 1, 2027... His name is Ashiss Dash.
Q1 revenues were at $5,082 mn, increase of 1% sequentially and 2.4% Y-on-Y in constant currency terms. Acquisitions contributed approximately 1.1% sequentially.

Large deal wins were strong at $3.6 bn with high net new of 61%, reflecting the relevance of our value proposition... We have been on the positive side of vendor consolidation with 20% of the total large deal TCV being from new vendor consolidation deals.
The lower end of the guidance assumes further deterioration in macro. Top end of the guidance assumes an improvement in macro, though lower than what we had assumed in April guidance.
pressing_questions: Why decide to leave at a time like now, instead of perhaps looking at an extension? And with the new CEO coming in, any mandate for the new CEO that you could highlight for us more clearly?

On the earnings, what is the reason for this revision downwards - where is the weakness? Where is momentum picking up? Some of your competitors like Tech M have been talking about irrational competitive pricing. Wipro has also spoken about that a bit. So what are you seeing in the environment?
With a 1% kind of growth in the first quarter, do we assume the second half will be meaningfully better if you were to reach that upper end of the 3% guidance?

Two of your peers have highlighted that AI revenue is slightly lumpy and it could be 1 or 2 quarters post which you will have to go and get those deals again. So is that something that Infosys is also seeing?
Would Infy ever at all, at least in the near future, would you want the company to move into the AI infrastructure business, data center, something that HCL and TCS has already done?
Infosys has lost some of the existing renewals, at least three in the know. What are the factors that led to that?
Could you quantify the AI-led deflation, if you can? And lastly, how do we define AI-led revenues?

With big tech getting into AI services space, will Indian IT companies end up becoming subcontractors at the end of the day, if these guys get into the game? And if that happens, will that rob you from the bigger opportunities in the AI space?

Tariffs and ongoing Middle East conflict are causing delayed decisions.
Focus on cost optimization and operational resilience.
Near term and FY27 growth will be impacted due to low revenue from one large client.

subsections.label: Retail & Communications
points: Retail budgets are tightly controlled, with discretionary spending under pressure.
Clients want AI productivity to do more with similar budgets and expect demand for AI-assisted legacy modernization.

quarters.summary: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd anticipates over 10% volume growth in FY27, supported by capacity additions and demand, while managing geopolitical and supply-chain risks.

subsections.label: Sequential margin bridge (Q4 vs Q3)
points: Employee cost +100 bps (benefit) due to prior quarter one-time labor code provision.
Lower discounts +50 bps.
FX tailwind +30 bps.
Fixed cost absorption +50 bps from inventory accretion.
Commodities -80 bps.
New model expenses -60 bps.
Other expenses -20 bps (CSR/R&D seasonality/lumpiness).

subsections.label: Other income / mark-to-market mechanics
points: CFO quantified rate impact: ~46 bps blended benchmark move in the quarter drove ~INR 750 cr sequential hit (and INR 1,075 cr YoY hit).
Reversal is dynamic: “As of yesterday, some amount of reversal has already happened. Roughly about 35% of this is already reversed.”
Credit quality remains conservative: “more than 99.5% AAA-rated security.”

subsections.label: Industry context and demand shaping
points: H1 FY26: PV market -0.4% YoY, attributed to “affordability pressures, particularly in the small car segment.”
H2 FY26: sharp rebound +16.7% YoY, “led by the government's GST reform,” with recovery “clearly led by the small car segment, particularly vehicles in the 18% GST bracket.”
Maruti’s domestic performance showed greater cyclicality than industry: Domestic sales -5.6% in H1, then +12.3% in H2, a “swing of about 17.9%.”

subsections.label: Key strategic/product developments
points: Small car/18% GST segment regained momentum, with management noting that despite SUV-heavy market structure, “the top-selling passenger vehicle… was the Dzire” (18% GST bracket).
Mid-SUV push strengthened via VICTORIS: “Fastest model in mid-SUV to cross 50,000 cumulative sales.”
Won Indian Car of the Year, supporting brand momentum in a high-growth segment.

subsections.label: EV entry
points: Launched first BEV e VITARA: Positioned as “first fully electric SUV developed on a fresh dedicated platform” for India and “about 100 global markets.”
“Initial response has been quite encouraging,” but management said EV volumes are currently production constrained; near-term priority is “100% customer delight” (delivery experience, home chargers).
Management also flagged EVs as a structural tailwind to ASPs: “EVs have to increase in the future. So that will help ASPs.”

subsections.label: Safety as a portfolio-wide commitment
points: “6 airbags as standard in almost all” lineup (volumes “beyond 99%”).
ESC and ABS+EBD standard across lineup.
Bharat NCAP: 5-star for all-new Dzire, VICTORIS, e VITARA, Invicto; Baleno 4-star.

subsections.label: Charging ecosystem buildout
points: ~2,000 exclusive charging points across sales/service in 1,100 cities.
Partnered with 13 charge point operators; target is “over 1 lakh charging points across India by 2030” (with dealers/CPOs).

subsections.label: Inclusive mobility feature
points: Launched WagonR with swivel seat option to aid seniors/persons with disabilities, aligned to “By Your Side” and UN SDG inequality reduction.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion and supply-side execution
points: Management framed recent GST reduction as “transformative,” improving affordability and placing the sector on “sustained long-term structural growth.”
To address demand and backlog, Maruti is accelerating capacity: Kharkhoda plant Phase 2 and Gujarat (Hansalpur) 4th line both to be operational within FY27.
Each adds 250,000 units/year, i.e., ~0.5 million units/year in one year, which management called “virtually unheard of.”
Medium-term plan: increase capacity to 4 million units per annum.
Start-up costs: CFO expects no significant drag, as “economies of scale should be able to broadly take care of the start-up cost,” assuming demand remains supportive.

key_figures.label: Export Share of India's Total PV Exports

subsections.label: Exports: scale leadership, but near-term uncertainty acknowledged
points: FY26 exports hit a record 447,000 units; Q4 exports also at record 137,215 units.
Maruti highlighted export dominance: the company “alone contributed 49% share of India's total passenger vehicle exports.”

On FY27 exports, management explicitly avoided numeric guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty: “If you can help me predict the war, I can predict the export number,” while aiming for “at least the last year numbers.”

subsections.label: Geopolitical / supply-chain risk management and cost pressure posture
points: Management cited complex operating conditions: “supply issues in rare earth metals,” West Asia conflict affecting “energy, certain raw materials and logistics.”
Mitigation actions emphasized: Preventing production disruption (gas supply, alternate fuels, diversification).
Sourcing commodities at “lowest possible cost,” supplier coordination, contingency planning.
Leveraging strong demand and utilization (pending orders support throughput).
View on persistence: pressures acknowledged but treated as manageable—“some cost headwinds do come and it's part of business”—with expectation they could ease when the crisis abates.

subsections.label: Outlook signals (FY27)
points: Volume growth ambition is company-specific: management indicated expectation of “growth of over 10% this year” (Maruti), supported by capacity additions and demand.
FY27 capex: CFO guided ~INR 14,000 cr for the year.
Inventory (balance sheet) uptick explanation: mainly raw materials and WIP, plus goods in transit, positioned for “ramping up the capacity in the coming 2 quarters,” not a finished-goods build.

Strategic portfolio broadening: credible mid-SUV momentum (VICTORIS) plus first BEV (e VITARA) and charging partnerships position Maruti for mix/ASP uplift, though EV volumes remain capacity constrained in the near term.

quarters.summary: Bajaj Auto achieved record performance in Q1 FY27 despite operational disruptions, with strong growth in exports and electric vehicles. The company plans to expand capacity and focus on premium and electric segments.

subsections.label: Cost & Margin Management
points: CFO called Q1 'hyperinflationary' with commodity inflation rising to ~4.5% of revenue.
Specific increases cited: steel +10%, aluminum/platinum +~40%, rhodium +~40%, plus ABS, copper, nickel, natural rubber.
Inflation broadened into electronics, proprietary components, energy, logistics, labor.
Pricing offset 'nearly about half' of inflation with pricing in Apr & Jun.
Additional offsets: rupee depreciation and discretionary cost rationalization.
Despite cost shock, EBITDA margin 20.9% (+10 bps QoQ, +110 bps YoY).

subsections.label: Capital Allocation, Balance Sheet, and Subsidiaries
points: Standalone FCF ~₹2,300cr (≈80% of PAT); surplus cash ₹21,000cr at quarter-end.
Shareholder returns: CFO clarified July outflows include dividend + recently concluded buyback.
Total payout aligned to prior commitment of 100% payout of FY26 profit (~₹9,825cr).
Cash expected to dip post-July and rebuild toward ~₹15,000cr by FY-end.
Consolidation: Q1 consolidated includes first full quarter of Bajaj Mobility AG, reducing YoY comparability.
Consolidated revenue ₹21,689cr (+65% YoY); consolidated PAT ₹3,226cr (+46% YoY).
Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL/BACM): income ₹1,100cr+, PAT ₹227cr (>2x YoY); AUM ~₹20,000cr (+70% YoY); CAR 19%; ROE >25% (as of Jun 2026).

subsections.label: Forward View
points: Export run-rate ambition: move beyond '250,000 per month' from Q2 onward (vs ~200k/month only a few quarters earlier).
Domestic 2W: portfolio 'turnaround program' and heavy launch calendar.

key_figures.label: EV and Export Contribution to Domestic Revenue

subsections.label: Segment Mix Shift
points: Management highlighted exports and EV as standout: 'Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double digit EBITDA percentage.'
EV profitability update (explicit): EV portfolio (2W+3W) remains 'double digit' EBITDA margin; Chetak moved from 'EBITDA neutral' to 'EBITDA positive.'
Exports: record volumes, broad-based share gains; aiming >250k/month.

subsections.label: Premium Exports
points: KTM exports from India recovered: +20% YoY; Triumph brand exports +40% YoY.

subsections.label: Domestic CV (3W incl. e‑rickshaws)
points: Industry (incl. e‑rickshaws) grew ~11% YoY; e‑autos doubled, now 44% of L5.
Bajaj delivered highest ever billings and retail; ICE share ~70%; EV leadership maintained.
L3/e‑rickshaw: new product 'RICI' in ~150 cities; company frames L3 as upgrade opportunity via quality/reliability/ownership experience.
Noted: L3 segment highly disorganized and largely lead-acid; regulatory pressure is limiting lead-acid permits; this is expected to drive lead-acid → Li-ion migration and upgrading.

subsections.label: Near-term Launch Blitz
points: Within ~6 weeks: complete 'exhaustive portfolio makeover' with:
'an absolutely new 150cc under the Pulsar brand'
'10 facelifts in the 160 to 400cc range' with 'class-leading features,' more electronics, and improved engine performance
'an absolutely new 125cc' Pulsar + upgrades

Later in FY27: introduce 'two new brands in the 125cc segment' (new nameplates, not Pulsar), with differentiated propositions; strategic aim includes upgrading 100cc customers into 125cc where innovation headroom and profitability are better.

subsections.label: Capacity Management
points: Capacity is now the binding constraint; plan to expand ~25% from 7mn to ~9mn units/year focused on EV 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, and 3Ws.
Demand exceeds supply; capacity: currently ~50k/month, immediate unlock to ~60k/month via productivity/vendor actions; broader capacity expansion underway.

subsections.label: Africa
points: Industry grew ~50%; Bajaj grew ~2x that; retail 'doubled,' led by Boxer 125 Heavy Duty (upgrade).
Nigeria: pre-election institutional demand; Bajaj claims it captured disproportionate growth with ~60% retail market share; driven by Boxer equity and 'wide footprint of retail and service network.'

subsections.label: Latin America
points: Continued strong outperformance, especially Mexico (noted as 'amongst the top five markets of the world').
Drivers: success of NS / N250 models, 'well-organized supply chain in Mexico' and favorable tariffs (management cited 3%), plus distribution expansion (75 stores).
Region also positioned as a driver of 'corporate capital' (i.e., profitability/cash).

subsections.label: Asia
points: Muted due to Bangladesh/Nepal; focus shifted to defending share and dealer health.
Philippines: multiple launches + exclusive motorcycle stores to build the premium/personal motorcycling category.

subsections.label: Supply Disruptions Quantified
points: Multiple concurrent shocks: industrial fuel supply curtailment, West Asia logistics force majeure impacting alloys/polymers, labor shortages due to cost-of-living + elections.
Estimated lost production opportunity: ~10% of volume.

subsections.label: Industry Context (Demand Shape)
points: Domestic 2W registrations +14% YoY (Q1), slower than Q4 (+25%); growth led by EV scooters and 150–400cc motorcycles.
100cc & 125cc segments were 'flattish,' resulting in ~7% industry motorcycle growth.

Management interpretation: stress is concentrated 'down the pyramid'; higher-income cohorts remain stronger. They explicitly linked sentiment drag to West Asia crisis and household fuel pressures ('LPG availability into every kitchen').

subsections.label: Bajaj Strategy: De-emphasize 100cc on Profitability Grounds
points: Clear positioning: in 100cc, Bajaj will participate 'at our own terms,' and where 'growth and profitability… get into a conflict… we tend to favor profitability and are prepared to lose market share.'
Rationale: 100cc structurally shrinking (management cited industry mix decline from ~55% to mid‑40s over 5–7 years) and low 'degrees of freedom' for innovation.

Continue scaling and performance in BACL.

quarters.summary: Eicher Motors Ltd anticipates continued demand growth, with strategic capacity expansions and a focus on premium motorcycle segments, while navigating commodity inflation and geopolitical uncertainties.

subsections.label: Demand and channel health
points: Management sees sustained structural demand; explicitly: 'there is no structural correction… demand… continuing.'

Premium motorcycle segment expansion: Govindarajan described premiumization as persistent: 'only the premium segment is growing,' with the premium market expanding from ~70,000/month (FY22/23) to ~1.1 lakh/month now, and RE contributing ~90,000+ of that.
April momentum: Reported April sales ~1.04 lakh, '57% growth' YoY (also referenced strong momentum/'growth of 51%' at one point).

Inventory tightness: Dealer + depot inventory '7, 8 days'; dealer inventory even lower. Short-term constraint attributed to temporary disruptions: 'manpower availability due to elections and LPG shortages' (week-to-10-day phenomenon), now 'back on track.'

key_figures.label: Eicher brand HD trucks market share

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Demand, mix, product actions, and electric entry
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Electric (Flying Flea) entry and commercialization approach
points: Entry into EVs positioned as brand expansion: Flying Flea described as a 'City Plus electric mobility brand.'
Launch: Flying Flea C6 launched in Bengaluru (first week of April 2026) with 'very exciting' response.
Go-to-market: Highly controlled ramp—'deliberate city-by-city approach', currently one store; management stressed 'we are not in a rush' and avoided volume targets.
Product/brand validation signals cited: C6 won the Red Dot Award pre-launch; media ride feedback 'journalists really, really love the motorcycle.'

subsections.label: VECV: Segment performance, market share progress, and EV traction
points: Eicher brand HD trucks: 25,155 units (+14.1%), market share improved to 9.1%.
LMD trucks: 46,195 units, management claimed leadership with emphasis that leadership must pair with 'profitable growth.'
New segment (SUV / small commercial EV platform): 2,452 Pro X delivered including 726 EVs—called out as opening 'an important new avenue for growth.'
Buses: Eicher buses 18,651; Volvo buses record 712.
Volvo trucks: 1,712.
Exports: +33.9% to 6,933 units despite 'challenging external environment.'
Aftermarket: Spare parts sales +13.9% to INR3,045.5 cr (notable scale and growth).

subsections.label: Product portfolio and pipeline (ICE)
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Capacity expansion roadmap (key operational lever)
points: Near-term debottlenecking: Current declared capacity ~1.4 million; additional '500 module per day' kicking in June/July raises run-rate to '~1.6 million plus.' Clarified as per-day modular capacity across facilities; effectively brownfield debottlenecking.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion: INR958 cr capex announced; targeted to lift total annual capacity to ~2.0 million by 'Q2 of FY28.'

Greenfield land bank and timeline: Andhra Pradesh greenfield—MoU signed for 261 acres to support future growth beyond 2.0 million. Tentative execution window shared: '24 to 30 months… fully operational' after land and business case finalization.
Strategic rationale: management framed land as the longest lead-time bottleneck—'The longest lead time is always… land parcel in hand.'

subsections.label: Major strategic development: Proposed Volvo JV for captive vehicle financing
points: Eicher disclosed intent to set up a 50:50 JV with Volvo for 'financing, leasing and other financial services business.'
Capital commitment: Eicher investment 'up to INR750 crores for the 50% stake' into Volvo Financial Services India (VFS India) via fresh equity infusion.
Base business scale: VFS India operating 10+ years with AUM INR1,806 cr and net worth ~INR500 cr (as per management Q&A).

Purpose and positioning: Designed as a 'captive financing arm for VECV, EML and Volvo Group products in India.' Meant to improve conversion and customer experience: 'using financing as a lever for… superior customer experience.'
Volvo brings global product capability; Eicher brings distribution and market knowledge to capture business 'in a more aligned and efficient manner.'
Pacing / risk stance: Management emphasized controlled growth and underwriting discipline—JV will be run 'absolutely independently' with decisions based on 'risk profile.'

Capital runway / medium-term AUM aspiration (management math): With additional capital, leverage capacity (they referenced D/E up to 5:1) could support scaling to ~INR9,000–10,000 cr AUM over ~5 years, and 'we don’t think… additional money at least for the next 5 years.'

Notable change: Vinod Aggarwal stated this is the first time Eicher has 'seriously evaluated entering this business,' enabled by the maturity of the Volvo partnership and Volvo’s global financing success.

subsections.label: Margins, commodity inflation, and pricing actions (key investor debate)
points: Q4 FY26 (RE / EML commentary): CFO quantified Q4 commodity impact: ~90 bps margin headwind.
Pricing action: January price increase delivered ~70 bps; residual ~20 bps mitigated via value-driven cost reduction and mix/model price variance.

Q1/FY27 setup: 'war situation' operating environment and mitigation levers Govindarajan described current environment as 'complex because of the war situation' creating both inflation and availability constraints.
Expected commodity headwind: '~3% to 3.5% on the material cost level impact… incremental in Q1.'

Pricing: RE took ~1.75% price increase in April; management implied roughly ~50% recovery of the inflation via price, remaining to be addressed through: accelerated value engineering / cost reduction ('front ending' projects into July/August), austerity measures, and pre-buy and inventory strategies ('we also have done some prebuy'). Management also confirmed operating leverage is an additional mitigant.
VECV pricing response: VECV announced ~2% price increases effective 1 April, alongside ongoing value engineering, commodity optimization, and transaction price improvements.

subsections.label: Industry and demand outlook: Management stance, headwinds, and confidence markers
points: No formal numeric guidance provided for FY27 volumes/industry, but tone remained constructive: RE: strong inquiry/booking rates; 'working on fulfilling the demand.' VECV: 'traction… quite good,' but environment 'dynamic' with 'global uncertainties… supply chain volatility.'
Short-term disruptions: Elections-driven labor migration and LPG availability created ~2–3 weeks of disturbance; management indicated normalization over recent days with production 'back.'
Europe (RE): 'market adjustment year' with industry degrowth and OBD2B pre-registered inventory overhang slowing fresh billings; RE claims to be holding share in a declining market.
US (RE): tariff-related uncertainty acknowledged but characterized as small exposure: 'only about 3% of the total market for us.'
Brazil: explicitly elevated as strategic growth engine—'Brazil is now our largest and the fastest-growing international market, second only to India,' with ~71% growth and product awards.

Launch markets include UK, France, Italy, Germany, Spain, India, and later the US.
Atlas/Atlas GT positioned in adventure and sport touring segments.
Go-to-market strategy involves a mix of independent premium dealers and multi-brand premium outlets.
Strategic framing leverages British design engineering capability with Indian manufacturing excellence.

FY outlook guides industry growth in double digits for ICE; EV expected to remain strong with rising penetration.

Festive season/product cadence with planned launches in October and November.

International business (IB) Q1 sales: 4.68 lakh units, +33% YoY, described as “highest ever international business sales.”

quarters.summary: Management guided to strong single-digit domestic industry growth for FY'27 with TVS expected to grow ahead of industry, continued EV and scooter momentum, cautious near-term outlook (Q1-Q2) due to commodity inflation (3-5% of revenue) and supply chain/labor disruptions expected to ease within 2-3 weeks, and continued capex/investment behind capacity expansion, Norton, R&D and new product launches including Hyundai-TVS 3-wheeler EV JDA.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory

Improvement driven by scale benefits, better product mix, premiumization, 3-wheeler and international business strengthening realization per vehicle, and cost leverage/amortization of fixed costs over larger base.
Management declined to give explicit margin guidance, stating pricing is only one lever alongside value, TCO, technology and connectivity, and variant strategy.

subsections.label: Investment breakdown FY26
points: Of the INR2,400 crores total investment in FY26, the predominant share was for overseas subsidiary Norton, with products readying for Q2 FY27 launch.
INR200 crores invested in TVS Credit Services.
Strategic investment in Dubai (~INR300 crores) to build infrastructure focused on international markets.

subsections.label: FY27 investment/capex outlook
points: Investments (Norton, TVS Credit, Dubai-type items) expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (i.e., INR500-600 crores lower), as many earlier investments are expected to start yielding revenues/results.
New investment opportunities beyond Norton/Dubai/TVS Credit could arise, to be disclosed closer to decision.

Total capex for TVS Motor in FY27 estimated at ~INR3,500 crores, comprising ~INR2,000 crores product development, ~INR1,000 crores+ capacity expansion (1.5 million unit addition), and additional R&D/testing investment.
