key_takeaways: Q1 was the highest ever first quarter performance for UltraTech across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit.
Domestic grey cement volumes grew 13.1%, capacity utilization improved to 81% from 76%, EBITDA of INR5,146 crores and PAT of INR2,604 crores, up 17.2% YoY.
Kesoram and India Cements brands have been converted to 100% UltraTech; the converted brand grew 21.3% YoY as B/C category customers migrated to the A category UltraTech brand at a price premium.
Operating EBITDA per ton held steady above INR1,200 despite the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory, reflecting cost discipline and operating leverage.

India Cements delivered a clear turnaround: like-for-like revenue grew 21% and volumes grew 19%, with EBITDA per ton climbing sequentially from INR386 (Q2FY26) to INR400, INR509 and INR603 (Q1FY27); India Cements EBITDA per ton of INR1,000 remains targeted by Q4 FY28.

Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons and total capacity 205.5 million tons after commissioning of Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu; consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons in 2-2.5 years backed by ~INR17,000 crores capex.
Cables and Wires project remains on schedule and on budget, reaffirming commissioning and product launch in Q3 FY27.
Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.87x from 0.94x at start of year, and company remains confident of ending FY27 below 1x.
Q2 FY27 expected to be optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and full quarter impact of West Asia cost disruption, with an expected INR130-140 per ton cost increase.
pressing_questions: What is the sort of working capital days for the Cables and Wires business, particularly on inventory days given the low lead distance from suppliers like Hindalco?
What steps remain before India Cements could be merged into a stand-alone entity, given most acquisition targets are nearing completion?
Given industry players revisiting expansion plans, what is UltraTech's estimate of industry-wide capacity addition for FY27-28?
Is there a structural shift toward prioritizing profitability/pricing over market share, or vice versa, if input costs decline later in the year?
How cement-intensive are river-linking projects like Ken-Betwa compared to something like a hydropower plant?

quarters.summary: UltraTech expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum in FY27 and beyond, targets double-digit volume growth for UltraTech itself in FY27, plans capex of INR8,000-10,000 crores every year for the foreseeable future to grow beyond 240 million tons capacity (37 million tons already committed to take capacity to 242.5 million tons by FY28), and expects cost-efficiency programs (India Cements/Kesoram) to push India Cements EBITDA/ton beyond INR1,000 by FY28, with near-term cost headwinds from the West Asia conflict (fuel, bags, forex) being managed via pricing and sourcing measures; leverage to be maintained below 1x.

points: INR800 crores spent out of committed INR1,800 crores capex for the cable and wire business.

subsections.label: India Cements / Kesoram integration progress
points: Sequential improvement in India Cements EBITDA per ton every quarter since acquisition (INR305 in Q3 to INR497 in Q4).
India Cements declared PAT of INR60 crores for the quarter, first time in a long time.

Under a related-party tolling arrangement, India Cements manufactures and sells the UltraTech brand but does not bear direct marketing/distribution costs — those sit at the UltraTech consolidated level, with UltraTech charging a markup per bag on ICL volumes to offset this; hence India Cements' underlying operational progress is understated by the reported INR497/ton figure (true comparable figure ~INR670/ton after accounting for the INR200/ton booked in UltraTech books).
Selling price improvements in southern markets expected to give India Cements further boost.
Kesoram already operating at ~INR1,000/ton EBITDA, broadly in line with other South cement operations.

India Cements and Kesoram together represent ~13% of consolidated capacity, moving from an integration drag to an earnings contributor; expected to become a meaningful and growing source of group-level EBITDA accretion as cost-improvement capex matures.
100% brand migration completed by end of March 2026 for both India Cements and Kesoram, a quarter ahead of schedule.

Post full brand conversion, only ~0.5 million tons of India Cements volume in Q4 remained non-UltraTech branded (0.39 million tons), implying limited further realization upside purely from brand conversion but significant efficiency upside from logistics/operational integration (single product now shipped from all 9 India Cements factories vs multiple brands earlier).
Efficiency improvement of INR200/ton still expected to flow into India Cements' books; full efficiency program (targeting >INR300/ton) to mature further into FY28.
India Cements EBITDA/ton guidance of >INR1,000/ton by FY28 is described as 'all inclusive' — i.e., includes the ~INR200/ton currently booked in UltraTech's standalone books via the tolling markup.

subsections.label: UAE / overseas operations
points: UAE capacity utilization dropped to ~80% during the war from 100% pre-war; now recovering with 'permanent peace program' in place, with utilization and prices both moving up.
UAE operations are entirely bulk (no bag costs) and 100% sold to RMC (zero trade sales).
Stable sequential UAE EBITDA (INR267 crores Q3 to INR278 crores Q4) — described as a 'stable journey'.
UAE economy expected to be among the first to recover, potentially with new government programs reviving the economy.

subsections.label: RMC business
points: RMC considered an integral, strategic part of UltraTech's business and offering, viewed as the future growth engine given increasing urbanization.
No specific numeric target set for RMC's share of volumes (currently 3%); no plan to monetize the RMC business.
RMC revenue growth outpacing volume growth.

subsections.label: Capacity growth trajectory
points: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India — a first for any company in a single country outside China.

Reached 100 million tons in 2019, added 50 million tons over 5 years to reach 150 million by 2024, then went from 150 to 200 million tons in less than 2 years — a full year ahead of the company's own targets.
More than tripled capacity in a decade, from ~65 million tons in 2016 to 200 million tons today.
Outside China, UltraTech is the largest cement company globally by sales volume and the only company anywhere with over 100 million tons of production capacity within a single country.
Committed to add a further 37 million tons in a phased manner, taking total capacity over 242.5 million tons by FY28.

Company has already begun charting its growth story beyond 240 million tons capacity, with further details to be shared next year; incremental capex beyond 240 million tons estimated at plus/minus INR15,000 crores.

subsections.label: Green energy and fuel mix
points: Renewable energy platform has been growing from strength to strength; ~43% of power needs currently met from green sources.
Company committed to reaching ~85% of power requirements from green energy by end of FY30 and is confident of achieving this.
On the fuel side, actively managing the mix by optimizing between petcoke, coal, alternative fuels, and increasing domestic coal share wherever possible.

No new thermal power capacity being added; instead, higher levels of WHRS (waste heat recovery systems) are being added, along with tying up renewable energy, aided by grid availability at several locations.

subsections.label: Logistics / lead distance
points: Lead distance reduced to 367 km, aided by an ever-expanding bulk terminal network including the new Lucknow facility, helping reach customers faster and reduce overall costs.

subsections.label: Clinker factor
points: Clinker conversion ratio currently at 1.48x, targeted to reach 1.54x by fiscal '28.
Company will always remain fully clinker-backed (maintaining historical hypothesis of 70% clinker backing) even as conversion ratio improves.

Management declined to comment on industry-wide clinker conversion trends but noted UltraTech is structurally stronger than the rest of the industry across multiple metrics including EBITDA/ton and growth.

subsections.label: Regional notes
points: Mumbai infrastructure spend of $60 billion cited as a structural demand driver going forward, with 2035 expected to represent a totally new phase for the city.
Western region infra demand expected to turn 'darker green' (i.e., stronger) going forward given large infrastructure spend plans.
India Cements' logistics efficiency set to improve now that a single (UltraTech) product ships from all 9 India Cements factories, versus multiple brands shipping earlier.

subsections.label: Sourcing and mitigation measures for West Asia crisis
points: Company dispatches have not suffered at any location due to the conflict; bag availability has become expensive but has not been a crisis.

Mitigation measures include diversifying procurement sources, identifying new sourcing opportunities, and entering long-term fuel contracts that are expected to be favorable going forward (unlike unfavorable long-term contracts over the last 2 years).
~150 bag suppliers across the country provide sourcing resilience; high-volume customers like UltraTech get prioritized servicing from suppliers.
Diesel price impact remains uncertain and unquantified; management states it will 'wait and watch'.

Some ripples in fuel costs expected in July-September if pet coke prices sustain at elevated levels ($150-160), but company expects to manage better than industry peers due to supply contracts and domestic coal sourcing.
Long-term fuel supply contracts and inventory/sourcing rotation are continuous and expected to persist as a mitigation lever.
Bag cost increase from INR9 to INR15 per bag (delta of INR6) has already occurred; cost has since stabilized/slightly reduced to INR13-14 per bag.
INR90 crore bag-cost hit in March cannot be annualized, as prices have since stabilized and volumes of alternate inventory/sources have been built up.

subsections.label: Premiumization and market positioning
points: Blended cement share and premium portfolio contribution both moved higher during the quarter — a conscious, deliberate strategy going forward.
UltraTech enjoys premium brand positioning, which has helped realizations especially post brand migration of acquired assets (India Cements, Kesoram).
Cement industry has been relatively slower than other building material industries (steel, agri, PVC) in taking price hikes, attributed to industry fragmentation.
UltraTech outperforming the rest of the industry in growth and EBITDA per ton, attributed to clinker conversion improvements (composite cement), RMC integration, and other operational efficiencies.

subsections.label: India Cements legal/merger status
points: Merger of India Cements into UltraTech not yet undertaken due to legacy, long-pending legal cases; management is working to resolve these before proceeding to next phase of integration, to avoid any risk to the main UltraTech Board/company.
No specific timeline provided for full merger.

subsections.label: RCB / balance sheet ring-fencing
points: Management reaffirmed that UltraTech's balance sheet remains ring-fenced and not used to support other group entities (referencing prior Chairman statements made regarding Vodafone-Idea aspersions); no funds have moved from UltraTech's balance sheet for other purposes.
Operating cash flow is committed to meeting UltraTech's own capex requirements (~INR10,000 crores/year for at least 4-5 years, ~INR50,000 crores cumulative) and rewarding shareholders.

subsections.label: Adjacency/diversification stance
points: Wire and cable business remains the sole non-cement adjacency investment; management stated no other building-material-adjacent investments are planned for the next 5 years.

subsections.label: West Asia conflict impact
points: Conflict in West Asia is a real headwind on fuel costs, packing bags, freight, certain import-dependent supply chains, and near-term sentiment in some demand segments.
Rising oil prices could lead to increases in domestic petrol/diesel prices.
Government's monthly economic review for March '26 acknowledged the outlook has become slightly uncertain.
Management characterizes the West Asia situation as a near-term cost moderator, not a structural demand reversal.
Steel prices have seen volatility while cement prices have been largely stable (0-5% movement) over the last financial year.

subsections.label: Currency / forex risk
points: Rupee devaluation created a mark-to-market hit on $950 million of foreign-currency borrowings (fully hedged) due to accounting requirement at quarter-end rate (INR94.85/$ on 31 March vs. subsequent strengthening to below INR93), resulting in a noncash debit to EBITDA/P&L.
Management is not factoring in a scenario of dollar reaching INR100, calling any such move a notional debit risk to the P&L.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Packaging (bag) costs rose sharply in March (INR9 to INR15/bag, later stabilizing to INR13-14).
Diesel cost impact is unresolved and could surface in the coming months.
Fuel costs could see 'some ripples' in July-September if elevated pet coke prices persist.

subsections.label: Legal/legacy risk (India Cements)
points: Long-pending legacy legal cases inherited with India Cements are delaying full merger; company avoiding taking risk with the main UltraTech Board while working to resolve them.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Structural growth drivers (urbanization, government infra commitment, PMAY housing targets, rising rural demand) remain firmly in place and undiluted by the West Asia crisis.
Near-term environment complexities remain unpredictable ('nobody knows what will happen tomorrow'); management will 'wait and watch'.
Fiscal '27 P&L expected to start reflecting integration/cost-efficiency benefits from India Cements and Kesoram investments.
Company will maintain leverage below 1x net debt/EBITDA year after year even while meeting growth capex needs.
Future capex pipeline is described as fully funded with the growth story intact.

key_takeaways: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.

UltraTech is today the largest cement company in the world by sales volume outside of China, and the only cement company anywhere in the world to have over 100 million tons of production capacity within a single country.
Committed to add a further 37 million tons, which will take us over 242.5 million tons in a phased manner by fiscal '28.
Consolidated sales volumes has crossed a rocking 44 million tons this quarter; UltraTech as a brand year-on-year has grown 19%.
EBITDA per ton, excluding acquired assets, is at INR1,296 per ton for the quarter, up from INR1,225 in Q4 '25.

100% brand migration completed at the end of March '26 for both India Cements and Kesoram; India Cements EBITDA of INR497 per ton in Q4 '26 up from INR333 in Q2 and INR305 in Q3, and declared PAT of INR60 crores for the quarter, after a very long time.
Net debt-EBITDA of 0.94x at consolidated level and 0.92x at UltraTech India level; Board has recommended a dividend of INR240 a share for fiscal '26.

We expect a sustainable volume growth of 7% to 8% per annum; growth capex requirement is not shrinking, with a plan of investing around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores every year for the foreseeable future.

India Cements, you're doing the right things, when do we see the day when we actually merge it? I understand there are a few legal cases which are there. But any time lines over here?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw strong volume growth (18% YoY combined grey+white) driven by Central India expansion, with management guiding to ~22.5-23 million tons grey volume for FY27, continued double-digit growth, no change to capacity roadmap (40 million tons by FY28, 50 million by FY30), but near-term cost pressure (~INR150/ton in Q2 from fuel/diesel) expected to weigh on margins, with fuel cost expected to peak in Q2 before declining.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Net sale increase in Q1 FY27 was mainly on account of product mix and some price improvement.
EBITDA margin declined YoY and QoQ due to cost pressures (fuel, diesel) and operating deleverage from lower sequential volumes.

subsections.label: Cost pre-ponement
points: Q1 had a timing difference due to preponement of some maintenance (kiln), which will result in lower maintenance cost in Q2 versus what was earlier projected.
Pre-ponement of maintenance expense from Q2 to Q1 was in the range of INR50 crores.

subsections.label: Debt position
points: Net debt increased quarter-on-quarter as on 30th June 2026 compared to 31st March 2026, alongside a slight decline in cash balance and increase in gross debt.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Prices in Q1 were more or less flat/same versus average, as some price increase occurred in between the quarter.
Despite monsoon seasonality typically causing sharp price drops, management does not expect price drops this time due to cost pressures from the geopolitical situation.

subsections.label: Volume growth drivers
points: Major volume growth is driven by expansion in Central India, including the grinding unit in Bihar.
In existing markets of North and South, company continues to grow in line with the market as there is no extra volume/capacity available there.
FY27 growth may not fully sustain at Q1's pace due to capacity restrictions in North and South; growth engine remains Central India.
Company reiterated it will not lose market share in any region and plans to grow profitably rather than aggressively chase top-line with a strategic, brand-building approach.

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook (double-digit)
points: Management confirmed grey cement volume growth for FY27 will be double-digit, though North and South growth will be restricted by capacity limitations.
Console white cement double-digit growth may not be possible in FY27 due to loss of ~50% normal Middle East volume from geopolitical restrictions on shipping/loading.

key_figures.label: White business volume growth (implied via geopolitical tailwind)
Paint business revenue growth expected FY28

subsections.label: White cement/putty business
points: Geopolitical situation had a positive impact on white business as imports of white cement/putty from UAE into India did not come through, giving the company an opportunity for extra volumes.

Because white cement availability was limited (due to reduced UAE imports), the company could do extra volume; this positive impact was mainly seen in Q1, may continue partly in Q2, but competitive intensity in putty is expected to normalize/continue longer term.

The 0.6 MTPA putty capacity expansion at Nathdwara is nearing completion and expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27, reducing dependence on toll manufacturing amid peak demand challenges this quarter that required sourcing material from toll manufacturers.
Company plans to grow the putty business in double digits year-on-year but is capacity-constrained until Nathdwara commissioning.

subsections.label: RMC (Ready-Mix Concrete) business
points: RMC business ramping up from 5 plants exited in March to 17 operative plants currently, targeting 50 by FY27 and 100 by FY28.
RMC cost is largely captured under raw material cost consumed.
RMC is not a very high-EBITDA-margin business (4-7% standalone), but strategically necessary because losing RMC supply to a project risks losing associated cement and other building material volumes.
Marginal EBITDA loss currently in RMC as capacities ramp up; each plant takes about 3 months to reach breakeven; no significant loss expected, described as 'single-digit loss', not material.
First time RMC revenue was disclosed separately on a quarterly basis, as earlier volumes were insignificant (only 5 plants as of March exit).

subsections.label: Paint business
points: Entry into paint business was driven by need to diversify the paint counter beyond putty alone, as relying on one product was becoming difficult to retain customers.
Board approved a limited capital allocation of INR600 crore to the paint business, given priority on core cement business.
Paint business achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q1 FY27, ahead of the third-year breakeven expectation.
Paint business is expected to help/support putty volume growth, though the exact incremental contribution from paint synergy is difficult to quantify.
Paint business uses the JK Cement/putty platform for distribution (common customers); JK Cement charges platform/service charges to the paint company for this.

Two brands used: Acro and Maxx; Maxx brand sales are included in standalone JK Cement top line, while Acro brand is a direct sale from the subsidiary; most of Q1 paint revenue (INR125 crore) sits in the standalone entity.
Company plans to fund paint business growth from its own earnings going forward, keeping capital reserved for the core cement business.

subsections.label: White cement UAE/GCC operations
points: Due to geopolitical situation, white cement sales are currently restricted to GCC countries only; unable to export to other regions due to lack of available ship loading.
Some competitor imports (clinker and cement) have started coming into UAE/India but not yet at normal quantities; management is watching this closely for Q2.

subsections.label: Ongoing capex projects
points: Greenfield project at Jaisalmer progressing well; confident it will be commissioned within targeted timeframe of H1 FY28.
Grinding unit at Bhatinda progressing well.
Land acquired for a second split grinding location in Punjab; work to start at that site as soon as possible.
Wall putty expansion in Rajasthan is near completion and expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Panna Line 2 kiln is being worked at an expanded capacity of 4 million tons; expected to achieve this in the current fiscal (FY27); no clinker shortage currently foreseen for Central India volumes.

subsections.label: Expansion schedule/confidence
points: Company reaffirmed no plans to reschedule or push back capacity expansion (40 million tons by FY28, 50 million tons by 2030), despite some competitors stepping back on capacity expansion.
Next phase of expansion beyond the current 40-million-ton program is being worked out; Board approval timing to be decided at an appropriate time keeping the 2030 target in view.

It is premature to give a definite Board approval date for next expansion phase given large ongoing capex; decision will factor in project completion timing and overall business/geopolitical environment; no postponement or delay currently anticipated unless uncertain geopolitical situation aggravates and impacts cash flow.

Decision on next clinker line: company may not wait until full Jaisalmer commissioning; a call could be taken closer to commissioning, likely by end of this fiscal or beginning of last quarter of FY27, after assessing balance sheet position.
In order of priority, the next expansion after Jaisalmer is expected to be Muddapur.
Saifco expansion timing beyond FY28 is not yet clear; company wants to first fully utilize existing capacity, secure approvals, and ensure existing business is profitable before planning further.

subsections.label: Maintenance shutdown
points: Q1 FY27 maintenance shutdown at kiln was a planned pre-ponement (not a sudden/forced shutdown), driven by early detection of a 'red spot' requiring maintenance ahead of schedule; kiln maintenance timing can typically vary by 1 to 1.5 months.

No volume loss occurred due to the maintenance because the company had a huge clinker stock; some minimal clinker purchase was made for the South plant due to maintenance, but this was a minimal quantity.
18% combined volume growth would not have been possible if the shutdown had been an unplanned/forced shutdown.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: Central India (including new capacity such as the Bihar grinding unit) is the primary driver of volume growth this quarter.
Company gained certain market share in Central India across major regions.
Company maintained (did not necessarily gain) market share in North and South regions.
Regional profitability and utilization levels are not shared/disclosed separately by management, other than confirming North/South operating near 85-90% effective capacity.

subsections.label: UAE / GCC white cement geography
points: White cement sales currently restricted to GCC countries only due to inability to secure shipping/loading for exports to other regions amid the Middle East geopolitical situation.
UAE region lost about 50% of normal white cement volume in Q1 due to these restrictions, impacting consolidated white cement growth potential for the year.

subsections.label: Fuel sourcing by region
points: Central India plants consume only domestic (Indian) coal; no petcoke or imported fuel used there.
North plants use a mix: Indian coal (where economical via rail; road movement not economical) supplemented by petcoke and alternate fuel.
South plant uses only petcoke and alternate fuel; Indian coal is not viable there and is not used at all.
Imported US coal (high calorific, cheaper at times) is used opportunistically when economics are favorable versus petcoke.
Fuel mix is not fixed and continuously evolves with geopolitical situation affecting availability and pricing; company adapts to keep fuel cost most cost-effective.

subsections.label: Cost outlook for Q2 FY27
points: Packaging cost expected to be flat to marginally lower in Q2 versus Q1.
Fuel cost expected to increase ~INR75-100/ton in Q2, expected to peak in Q2 before declining thereafter under current fuel environment.

Maintenance cost in Q2 expected to be similar to Q1, maybe marginally lower, as some kiln maintenance is still pending and will be taken up in Q2; this component is separate/not linked to the INR150 variable cost increase guidance.
Operating deleverage impact (over and above the INR150/ton cost guidance) is expected in Q2 due to lower sequential volumes from seasonality.
Railway bulk freight discount benefit is limited only to North plants (where rail facilities exist); Central India and South plant logistics are entirely by road.

Consolidated raw material cost per ton appears higher partly because consolidated numbers include dry-mix mortar business (UAE), which raises raw material cost without a corresponding volume addition to the dividing factor.
In Fujairah (UAE), freight costs increased because dispatch was limited to GCC region sales only; dry-mix mortar business is local and has no freight cost impact.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company aims to grow profitably rather than chase aggressive top-line growth, prioritizing long-term brand and market position establishment, especially as most incremental volume comes from Central India.
Some competitor imports (clinker/cement) have started entering the UAE/India white cement market but not yet at normal pre-disruption quantities.

subsections.label: Coal block operationalization
points: Company has two coal blocks; the larger one at Mahan has made good progress and is expected to start yielding coal by end of FY28.
The second (smaller) coal block is expected to follow roughly one year later.
Company has the option to sell fuel externally from these coal blocks and will evaluate strategy for coal sales as it progresses.

Key benefit expected: substantial reduction in fuel-related risk exposure, since domestic linkage coal is cheapest but supply-constrained (especially impacting North plants); own coal block output expected to be cheaper than market-available domestic coal.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and cost risks
points: Ongoing geopolitical situation (Middle East) has affected fuel (petcoke, imported coal) pricing and availability, and has disrupted shipping/loading for white cement exports from UAE to non-GCC regions.

Potential risk to expansion timeline: if the geopolitical situation aggravates and impacts cash flow, there could be some delay to the next phase of capacity expansion, though currently no postponement is anticipated.
Green power capacity ramp-up has faced delays due to state-level approval delays for group power housing (solar), resulting in lower-than-expected green power contribution so far.
Thermal substitution rate target (35% by FY30) needs to be reworked because the original target was based on existing capacities before recent expansions and changes in fuel mix by location.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Management reiterated no plans to reschedule or delay the 40-million-ton (FY28) and 50-million-ton (2030) capacity roadmap, unlike some competitors pulling back on expansion.

Grey cement volume growth for FY27 confirmed to be double-digit, though overall pace may moderate versus Q1 due to capacity constraints in North and South; annual volume guidance is revised quarter to quarter.
Consolidated white cement volume growth may not reach double digits for the year due to the ~50% loss of normal UAE volume in H1 from geopolitical disruptions.

key_takeaways: During this quarter, we saw a good growth in the grey business, year-on-year 19% growth in volumes... and even though vis-à-vis previous quarter it was marginally lower by 2%.

Also, if we see the white business, year-on-year there is a growth of 11% in volumes, marginally lower by 5% Q-on-Q, and the combined growth in volumes was 18% year-on-year and marginal 3% down quarter-on-quarter.

As a result of this, the net sale during this quarter was higher by 23% year-on-year at INR3,786 crores as compared to INR3,068 crores... which was mainly on account of the product mix and some price improvement.

The EBITDA during this quarter was INR639 crores, this is the standalone position, vis-à-vis INR673 crores in the previous year and INR670 crores in the previous quarter. The EBITDA margins was 16.9% in this quarter, previous quarter 18.5%, and previous year 21.9%.
If we look at the work on the projects, the greenfield project at Jaisalmer is progressing well and we are confident that it will get commissioned within the targeted timeframe of first half of FY28.

As far as the debt profile as on 30th June, the gross debt stood at INR5,551 crores as compared to INR5,136 crores as on 31st March... The net debt is higher at INR3,864 crores as on 30th June compared to INR3,370 crores as on 31st March.
So the cost should go up by about say INR150 in Q2 as compared to Q1... overall, you know, with diesel and everything we expect that the cost should go up by INR150 a ton.

Yes, as of now we have no plans. We are on schedule. Once the 40 million is already in progress and immediately we shall -- we are already working out on the next phase of expansion...keeping our target for 2030.

Sir what was the exit utilization of Panna Line 2 in the quarter 1 FY27?

Sir, when we mention that we are looking at on the grey front 22.5 to 23 million ton kind of a volume for this year, that means we are looking at a very subdued growth for the next three quarters... don't we think we should be at least doing a 3 million ton extra volume in this year?

quarters.summary: JK Cement expects continued double-digit volume growth in FY27 (incremental ~2.5 million tons or more) with industry growing 6-8%, driven by capacity commissioning at Jaisalmer/Bikaner/Punjab (H1 FY28) and Nathdwara Wall Putty plant (September). Management remains confident on the 50-million-ton capacity roadmap by FY30 despite rising competitive intensity in Central and Rajasthan markets, though cost pressures from geopolitical situation (fuel, diesel) and moderating incentive income are headwinds; paints business expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27 on higher revenue.

subsections.label: Employee expense drivers
points: Commissioning of new plant in Central India led to salaries earlier capitalized moving to revenue expense.
Increased business requirement led to additional manpower requirement.
Normal annual increments had an impact.
Labor Code impact during the year was provided in this quarter.
One-time liability pertaining to leave travel assistance was provided in this quarter.

Management expects ~INR250 crores sustainable quarterly run rate; annual increment effective 1st April is ~10%; expects full year employee cost to rise 12%-14% YoY from INR937 crores base, partly due to Nathdwara plant commissioning in September requiring additional manpower.

subsections.label: Other expenses drivers
points: Other expenses increased due to higher business volumes, including packing costs, stores and spares, and variable selling expenses.
Increase also due to investment in branding for both gray and white cement businesses amid current market conditions, incremental ~INR50-60 crores.

subsections.label: Incentive income
points: Incentive income lower than earlier guidance of ~INR75 crores due to Aligarh unit exhausting its full 10-year incentive eligibility.
Rajasthan incentive not being availed because GST input credit is claimed instead (input credit received immediately, cannot claim both).
Q4 incentive accrued was INR29 crores; outstanding incentive receivable as on 31 March was ~INR300 crores.
Full year FY26 incentive was ~INR230 crores; FY27 incentive expected to be ~INR250-260 crores.
Bihar incentive not yet accrued pending sanction letter from state government; will be accrued (from back date) only after sanction letter received, per prudent accounting policy.
Incentives from other grinding units (Prayagraj, Hamirpur, etc.) expected going forward.
Incentive run rate may increase further in FY28 if quarterly run rate reaches INR70-75 crores, potentially reaching ~INR300 crores for FY28.

subsections.label: Capex plans
points: FY27 capex guidance of INR3,500-4,000 crores includes normal capex, Wall Putty plant capex, solar tie-up investments, Saifco/paints investments, and coal block investment — NOT the Jaisalmer expansion specifically as a separate line; out of this, normal capex is expected to be INR800-1,000 crores with balance on greenfield expansion.

FY28 capex guidance of INR1,500-2,000 crores is based only on commitments as on date; next expansion (after Jaisalmer) is on the cards but capex commitment will only be given once approved by the Board.

subsections.label: Panna project cost savings
points: Panna project has some spillover capex/expenditure remaining related to railway siding.
Out of the announced INR2,850 crores project cost, expected savings of at least INR200-250 crores, potentially up to INR300 crores, resulting in project completion at lower cost.

subsections.label: Cash balance
points: Standalone and consolidated cash balances are the same because subsidiaries (Saifco and Fujairah) hold hardly any cash balance.

key_figures.label: Consolidated White Cement volume growth expectation

subsections.label: Paints business
points: Paints revenue for FY26 was INR380 crores with an EBITDA loss of INR40+ crores.
FY27 revenue expected at INR500-550 crores (full year number, not exit run rate) with EBITDA expected to be positive/breakeven on the way, driven by improvement in gross margins and other factors.

subsections.label: White Cement / Wall Putty
points: White Cement was previously fed to certain South regions from UAE (Fujairah) plant as it was more economical; due to present geopolitical situation, this is now being fed from the Gotan plant instead — company does not expect to lose White Cement market share.
Prices for both White Cement and Wall Putty have been increased due to substantial increase in chemical input costs, with efforts to pass on cost increases to customers.

White Cement profitability (EBITDA per ton, including putty) not shared separately from gray cement; industry-wide White Cement profitability has been declining due to increased competition, but management expects it should not further reduce going forward.

subsections.label: Fuel mix and cost
points: Q4 fuel mix based on heat value: ~50% petcoke, 12% alternate fuels (AFR), balance Indian coal.

subsections.label: Project status
points: With Buxar commissioning, the total 6 million ton capacity expansion taken up in Central India is fully commissioned.
Muddapur plant capacity increased by 1 million tons via debottlenecking (South plant).
Work started on new greenfield project at Jaisalmer (7 million ton plant: 4 million ton integrated clinker + 3 million ton grinding), plus 2 million ton each grinding units at Bikaner and Punjab.
Integrated plant civil construction and erection work progressing well; orders for main plant and equipment at Bikaner already placed and construction begun.
For Punjab grinding unit, land already acquired, other approvals in process, order for main plant and equipment already placed.
Nathdwara Wall Putty plant work in advanced stage of completion.

subsections.label: Utilization and debottlenecking
points: Debottlenecking mainly done at South plant (Muddapur) increasing capacity from 3.5 to 4.5 million tons.
North remains the highest utilization region; expected to reduce slightly (4-5%) post new capacity commissioning but will remain higher than country average.
Central region combined expanded capacity utilization currently running at 65-75%.

subsections.label: Limestone / future expansion
points: Recently won limestone block in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana with 500 million ton reserves; being looked at for way forward to become a more national player; considered part of next phase of expansion (2030 plan) rather than immediate capacity addition.
No mining lease yet obtained for Odisha expansion; expansion plans will be considered once mining lease is granted.
For Saifco (Andhra), though mining lease is held, company will first stabilize position in market and plant, and start earning profit before considering expansion.
No immediate plan for expansion in Odisha or Saifco (Andhra) currently.

subsections.label: Green power / cost initiatives
points: Thermal power plants discarded (one at white cement, one at gray cement) as not economical to operate; will likely be sold as scrap; company moving towards more green power.
WHRS/green power share expected to increase by 2-3% in FY27 to ~55%, pending state government approvals and grid listing.
Major increase toward 75% green power target expected from FY28 onwards, contingent on commissioning of ~80 MW green power capacity currently in process.

subsections.label: Capacity roadmap confidence
points: Management confident of 2030 capacity plan and does not foresee change, though acknowledged that major cash flow challenges from geopolitical external factors could push the plan back by about 6 months.
Next expansion beyond Jaisalmer is on the cards and being planned; capex commitment guidance will only be given once Board approval is obtained.

subsections.label: Lead distance and logistics
points: Lead distance has come off quite a bit due to changed distribution; incremental volumes coming are all road-based (not rail-based) until new expansion (Jaisalmer) which will bring rail-based volumes.
Per ton per kilometer expected to be maintained overall while entering new areas, as each region has a different per ton per kilometer range.

Diesel price sensitivity: an increase to INR10-11 (from INR7 currently) could have an impact of about INR50-60 per ton; recent 8-10 INR/liter increase over past ~10 days has had limited impact so far (~INR10/ton), with further impact from yesterday's increase yet to be assessed.

subsections.label: Regional market dynamics
points: Central India market: peers alleged JK Cement pushing volumes in non-trade segment, subduing broader pricing — management clarified this feedback was from ~2 quarters back and that focus is on Key Account Management (KAM) as the major driver for volumes across regions, not just Central India, and company denies dumping material anywhere.

Rajasthan market: upcoming capacity additions from company itself (Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Punjab) expected to help serve market from shorter distances, improve market grip, and improve market share; company views this as an opportunity given previously only one effective source of supply (Nimbahera/Mangrol) served the region.
Punjab: no anticipated regulatory clearance issues currently despite a peer citing such issues and possible election-related slowdown; company would inform if issues arise.

subsections.label: Demand outlook and competitive positioning
points: Cement industry historically grows at 6-8%, an old formula suggested cement grows at 1.2x GDP growth, but company considers this conservative guidance appropriate given current geopolitical situation impacting many businesses, which could lead to deferred housing investment.

Jaypee plant's 5 million tons capacity becoming operational is not seen as a major competitive threat in Central market; company expects material volumes from Jaypee only from beginning of Q3, and management had already factored in intensifying competition (citing Dalmia's earlier unsuccessful attempt to seed the market).
Company is well prepared for increased competition in Rajasthan market with strengthened team/processes and plans to consolidate/strengthen position using new capacities.
Company denies dumping/discounting in non-trade segment in Central India; strategy is KAM (Key Account Management)-driven volume growth across regions.

subsections.label: Volume growth trajectory
points: FY27 incremental volume target raised from earlier 2 million tons/year to 2.5 million tons, with expectation to revise further to minimum 3 million tons/year going forward as part of 2030 plan, to justify return on capital investment.

FY28 incremental volumes similarly expected to be supported by Jaisalmer, Bikaner, and Punjab capacities coming online (particularly in second half), with potential extra volume if commissioning can be advanced by 2-3 months.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and cost inflation risk
points: Geopolitical situation impacting fuel costs and supply; company has secured new orders/planning up to September given uncertainty; expects it will take 3-4 months for situation to normalize.
Diesel price increases add further uncertainty; company aims to pass on cost increases to customers but the exact quantum of pass-through remains uncertain ('wait and watch').
Packing cost increase seen earlier due to sudden demand surge has since reduced substantially after alternatives were worked out.

Housing demand could be impacted if businesses face funding shortages/geopolitical pressures leading to deferral of housing investment; no major impact seen yet but factored into conservative demand guidance.
Major cash flow challenges arising from geopolitical external factors could delay the FY30 capacity roadmap by about 6 months, though management currently sees no such issue.

subsections.label: Regulatory risk
points: Peer companies reported regulatory clearance issues in Punjab, possibly linked to election-related slowdown; JK Cement does not currently foresee similar issues at its Punjab location but will inform if any arise.

subsections.label: Incentive-related risk
points: Loss of incentive eligibility for Nimbahera (North) due to inability to claim incentive when opting for GST input credit instead.

subsections.label: Cost savings initiatives
points: Major cost savings already achieved but ongoing; expect another INR50 per ton in FY27, mainly driven by green power and AFR (alternate fuels & raw materials) initiatives in South and North plants.

Cost savings guidance excludes benefit from newly installed waste heat recovery systems (only optimization of existing WHR counted); Central India ramp-up cost benefit will come through separately given cost advantage in that region, but timing of reflection not specified precisely.

key_takeaways: Net sales for Q4 increased by 15% QoQ at INR3,614 crores and 11% YoY; for the full year, net sales increased by 16% at INR12,568 crores as compared to INR10,802 crores.
EBITDA during the quarter was INR670 crores, up 25% QoQ but down 9% YoY; full year EBITDA was higher by 18% at INR2,318 crores.
EBITDA margins for the quarter were 18.5%, and for the full year were 18.5% versus 18.2% in the previous year.
Profit after tax was INR345 crores for the quarter, an increase of 91% QoQ but lower by 17% YoY; full year PAT was INR1,033 crores, an increase of 21%.
The Board proposed a dividend of INR20 per share, subject to shareholder approval.

During the quarter, the company commissioned the greenfield expansion at Buxar in Bihar, completing the total 6 million ton capacity expansion in Central India; also increased Muddapur plant capacity by 1 million ton to 4.5 million tons.

Work started on the new greenfield project at Jaisalmer (7 million ton plant) along with grinding units at Bikaner and Punjab, expected commissioning in H1 FY28; project cost for Jaisalmer integrated unit expected around INR3,630 crores with INR742 crores already spent up to March.
Gross debt as on 31st March is INR5,136 crores, net cash is INR1,765 crores, net debt is INR3,370 crores, net debt to EBITDA is 1.45, and net debt to equity is 0.48.
pressing_questions: Vaibhav Agarwal (moderator) followed up on whether JK Cement will continue with its 50 million ton capacity roadmap by FY30 given industry leaders like UltraTech now talking about 300-million-ton capacity while some peers hold back expansions, and management responded it is confident but flagged possible 6-month delay only if major cash flow challenges arise from geopolitical external factors.

A question was raised on peer feedback alleging JK Cement is pushing volumes in the non-trade segment in Central India, subduing broader pricing — management responded that this feedback was from about 2 quarters back and denied dumping material anywhere, emphasizing KAM (Key Account Management) as the volume driver.

subsections.label: Inventory “gain” mechanics (explicitly defined)

Management noted prices rose through most of Apr–mid Jun, with declines only late June—driving net gains.

Refinery-level gross GRMs (pre duties): Bina ~$57/bbl, Mumbai ~$34/bbl, Kochi ~$39/bbl.
Bina advantage attributed to crude slate flexibility: it can process “majority… high sulfur” crude, which was “comparatively cheaper than low sulfur.”

subsections.label: Marketing: margin pressure and pricing action
points: Elevated international product prices late in the quarter led to “adverse marketing margins.”
BPCL responded with “calibrated retail price revision of approximately ₹7.5/litre across MS and HSD” to partially mitigate losses in the latter part of the quarter.

subsections.label: Volume/mix commentary
points: Domestic sales volume 13.62 MMT; retail continuity: petrol/diesel supplies “largely uninterrupted.”

Non-retail/commercial diesel volumes dipped due to: shift from direct to retail; reduced volumes where BPCL would not sell below “standard margin”; and some product unavailability as refinery streams were diverted to LPG.

subsections.label: Retail & gas network expansion / productivity

subsections.label: LPG: supply constraints + anti-diversion controls + structural PNG shift
points: BPCL maintained LPG supply via diversified imports and maximized refinery LPG output; also implemented measures “under the government’s direction” to manage demand-supply.

Domestic LPG volumes fell ~14–15% (double-digit degrowth) in Q1, driven by: some supply shortage; tighter delivery/booking controls (“>90% digital bookings” and delivery confirmation via SMS); and PNG substitution (~30,000–40,000 connections surrendered from LPG as PNG expanded in connected areas).
Under-recovery per cylinder (CP-based snapshots): July CP under-recovery ~₹490/cylinder; with August CP $592, under-recovery about ₹210 (with caveat it may change if CP rises again).

subsections.label: LPG compensation: large and growing receivable buffer
points: As of June 30, 2026, cumulative LPG compensation buffer: ₹15,804 crore, after adjusting for installments received against the announced compensation of ₹10,594 crore.

subsections.label: Marketing segment momentum
points: Marketing business continued healthy momentum driven by steady demand growth across retail and commercial fuels.

BPCL continued to maintain leadership in throughput per retail outlet among PSU peers, strengthened by strategic marketing access, strong highway presence and continued focus on customer experience and retail productivity.
Retail segment expanded customer and infrastructure footprint during the year via new outlet commissioning.

On market share, management stated long-term strategy is to grow market share via network expansion and customer convenience initiatives rather than chase temporary gains; endeavor is to sustain market share over the long term even amid short-term fluctuations from current market conditions.
No shortage of fuels reported; credit policy to dealers continues, with restrictions applied only where customers default on repayment within the 3-4 day collection window.

subsections.label: LPG segment
points: LPG is a regulated product; management is hopeful of government support for under-recoveries as has occurred historically.

Actual LPG under-recovery estimated around INR650 per cylinder after accounting for higher freight (world scale rose from ~50-55 pre-war to 600-700 peak) and spot premiums of $200-300 over Saudi CP when term supply is unavailable.

Industry signed term contracts for ~10% of LPG requirement from US supplies, benchmarked at Saudi CP plus or minus $10-15 depending on freight; spot LPG cargoes from US now also being sourced via time-chartered vessels at higher landed cost than term.

subsections.label: Gas business
points: Gas business achieved 100% utilization of regasification capacity booking with Petronet LNG for the first time since inception of LNG imports by BPCL.

subsections.label: Upstream segment (Mozambique)
points: On 7 November 2025, operator informed Government of Mozambique that force majeure has been resolved; work resumed in full swing; first LNG cargo expected mid-2028.
First phase development is mostly under project finance with no equity commitment from BPCL going forward; future cash flow from first phase will be reinvested into subsequent phases.
Potential for future expansion phases exists beyond the current 13 TCF Phase 1 development.

subsections.label: Upstream segment (Brazil - BM-SEAL-11)
points: FPSO tender has been finalized and to be awarded shortly; FID approved by operator; first gas expected 2031-32; oil expected in 2031.
Delay in FPSO tender finalization (took ~3 years) caused project completion schedule extension to 2031-32.
This is currently one development in the field; potential exists for another development in the same field, but exploration/drilling still required and cannot be commented on at this stage.
BPCL's equity crude rights from Brazil can be brought to India or marketed elsewhere based on commercial considerations at the time.

subsections.label: Upstream segment (UAE)
points: Lower Zakum and Upper Zakum blocks are already producing with good volumes via India consortium's 10% stake.

Through SPV Urja Bharat Private Limited, first oil discovery in unconventional Shilaif play made in XN-76 well in UAE; BPRL also witnessed oil discovery during testing of exploration well XN-79 02S in Onshore Block 1.
New UAE discovery (completed FY26) will move to development plan stage; initial estimations suggest good reserves and extractable reserves, with details to be communicated once plan is ready.

key_figures.label: Andhra Pradesh refinery cum petrochemical project proposed capacity
Target own crude/profit-share volume from exploration projects

subsections.label: Strategic growth projects (Project Aspire)
points: Dearomatized Solvent project at Mumbai refinery commissioned in Q4 FY26 - a first-of-its-kind Make in India initiative that is an import substitution and strengthens presence in niche specialty products segment.

Krishnapatnam-Hyderabad pipeline commissioned in Q4 FY26, strengthening efficiency and providing critical evacuation infrastructure for upcoming projects, reflecting broader focus on logistics infrastructure.
During the year, company commissioned 2 retail depots, 2 LPG bottling plants, 3 aviation fueling stations and 2 gas pipelines to strengthen supply and distribution capabilities.
Irugur-Devangonthi and Mumbai-Rasayani pipelines under implementation to further strengthen supply chain resilience and network connectivity.

1G and 2G ethanol plants at Bargarh, Odisha commissioned in October 2025 and March 2026 respectively, aligned with national policy on biofuels aimed at enhancing energy security, reducing crude oil imports and promoting cleaner, greener fuels.

subsections.label: Bina Petrochemical and Refinery expansion
points: Schedule variance (23% actual vs 32% planned) primarily due to geopolitical developments and associated supply chain challenges affecting manufacturing and delivery.
Critical long lead items remain on track and all major packages have been awarded by February 2026.
Recent Middle East conflicts have impacted supply pricing and execution timelines; company is actively monitoring and implementing mitigation measures.

Total project cost INR49,800 crore, of which only INR6,500 crore is foreign component, limiting forex fluctuation impact; even a 10% INR depreciation would move this component to INR6,000-7,000 crore.
Around INR25,000 crore of tenders awarded on fixed-price contracts, limiting price impact on already-awarded work; ~20-25% of project work is yet to be awarded, carrying small potential cost impact.
Management expects to complete the project within plus or minus 10% of approved project cost.

subsections.label: Andhra Pradesh refinery cum petrochemical project
points: Key preparatory activities progressing as planned; environmental and technical studies completed, detailed engineering and financial appraisal activities underway.
Project supported by strong incentives from the Andhra Pradesh state government.

subsections.label: Other major projects
points: PRFCC project at Mumbai refinery, polypropylene project at Kochi, and POL and LOBS installation at Rasayani are progressing steadily in line with planned commissioning timelines.

PRFCC at Mumbai refinery: approved last year, work just started with licensor selection and BDEP ongoing; no major cost escalation foreseen at this point; clarity expected after 30-40% progress next year.

subsections.label: Renewable energy / green energy
points: Renewables give lower rate of return (8-9%) versus other investments, but are pursued to balance net-zero objectives with returns, primarily by using output within refineries rather than purchasing outsourced power.
2 gigawatt renewable target set for immediate period, with focus on maximizing in-refinery usage to improve effective returns.

subsections.label: Petrochemical integration strategy
points: Big potential advantage seen in integrating petrochemicals with refinery intermediaries for value addition, prompting petrochemical strategy adopted a couple of years back given limited prior presence in petrochemicals.
Petrochemical demand growth in India is 5-7%, with most petrochemical products currently import-driven, hence high petrochemical intensity planned in upcoming projects to meet domestic demand.

key_figures.label: Geographical regions covered by new grades
Spot crude share planned vs actual
Pre-war landed crude premium over benchmark (Brent)
Peak landed crude premium over benchmark (Brent), certain cargoes

subsections.label: Crude sourcing diversification
points: Increased Russian crude procurement from 25% in Q3 to 31% in Q4 to fill supply gaps amid the current geopolitical situation, and share continues to increase.
Diversified to 8 new grades of crude during the year covering 4 geographical regions.
Crude supplies secured through July 2026.
Other sourcing destinations include WTI, Venezuelan crude, and Middle Eastern spot grades like Murban; new grades tested last year included Venezuela, Brazil and Angola.

Term crude allocation planned at 55% of requirement at start of year, but only 45-46% of term requirement is being received due to constraints in the Strait of Hormuz; the resulting ~10% shortfall is being sourced via spot, pushing spot share to 55-60% versus planned 45%.
Major spot source currently is Russia.

Distillate yield will change if reliance shifts more toward WTI/Venezuelan crude (different API/assay), but this comes with commercial benefit; company balances crude mix based on value addition (GRM) and product demand; Venezuelan crude can only be processed as a blend in small cargo sizes with other grades, not directly.

Russian crude is not sanctioned itself—only certain entities are sanctioned (unlike Iran crude, which is sanctioned); BPCL only buys Russian crude via non-sanctioned entities (vessel owner, port, or supplier), consistent with practice even before the war.
Russian crude pricing has shifted from a discount scenario last year to a premium scenario currently, depending on demand-supply and sanctions status; not currently available at a discount.

subsections.label: LPG sourcing cost build-up
points: Two additional cost components explain higher-than-expected LPG under-recovery versus Saudi CP: (1) freight cost increase from world scale ~50-55 pre-war to 600-700 peak; (2) spot premiums of $200-300 when term contracts are unavailable, plus higher freight for US cargoes given ~90-day round-trip transit.

subsections.label: Inventory management
points: Company generally does not calculate refinery inventory gain/loss as average inventory is less than the purchase cycle, but during periods of large price fluctuation, inventory gains occur; management confirmed inventory gains helped refining margins in Q4 but declined to quantify.

Crude inventory maintained at 25-27 days generally (sometimes 1-2 days higher up to 28-29 days) due to preference for higher inventory levels; capped around 30 days due to storage/tankage constraints.
LPG inventory coverage fluctuates daily depending on cargo arrivals; comfortable range is 15-20 days but can dip below 15 days at times.

subsections.label: Retail market share strategy
points: Management does not pursue temporary market share gains from a conducive competitive environment (e.g., private players rethinking expansion amid uncertainty); long-term strategy is to sustain and grow market share via network expansion and customer convenience initiatives.
Objective is at least 32% retail segment market share over a couple of years, pursued through network expansion and initiatives to give more convenience to customers.

Management acknowledged a year of relative market share loss compared to peers but reiterated the priority is uninterrupted supply chain continuity — no customer should suffer due to non-availability of fuel — alongside continuous market expansion efforts.

subsections.label: Capital allocation philosophy
points: Objective of capital allocation is optimum returns to stakeholders while diversifying within and potentially beyond the energy sector, given the energy sector's modest 2-3% annualized growth.

Petrochemical integration with refinery intermediaries seen as a big value-addition opportunity given BPCL's historically limited petrochemical presence; major capital allocation now directed to petrochemicals.

Upstream capital allocation directed toward projects that have completed exploration and are moving to development, aiming for clarity on cash flows post-commissioning; target is 6-7 million metric tons of own crude oil rights/profit share against a refining capacity of ~41 million metric tons.

Capital discipline principle: projects are allocated capital only when commercial returns are clear; company targets projects with a 5-6 year payback (netback) period, where 80-90% of investment can be recovered in 4-5 years to reduce risk.
Debt-equity discipline: comfortable at 1:1 at peak during large project execution, normalizing to 0.4-0.5 after project commissioning; only then does the company take on the next large project.

subsections.label: Company milestone
points: BPCL is celebrating its 50th foundation year, having navigated multiple industry cycles.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and market risk
points: Ongoing tension in West Asia driving global and domestic economies through an uncertain phase, with major disruption in global energy supply chains impacting all sectors and geographical segments.
Crude and product prices, broadly range-bound for much of FY26, witnessed heightened volatility towards year-end amid disruptions to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.
Forex fluctuations and geopolitical developments continue to remain key drivers for energy markets.
Q1 FY27 flagged as a challenging period since the large impact of the war is not fully realized in Q4 FY26 due to timing differences.

Under-recoveries across products persist without a clear roadmap for recovery given deregulated status, though LPG (regulated) may receive government support as in the past; other products' under-recovery situation viewed by management as a short-term (not permanent) challenge, similar to prior episodes such as the Russia-Ukraine war.

If under-recovery situation persists for a longer period without price revisions, no balance sheet can fully absorb the impact indefinitely; some point requires burden-sharing among stakeholders via price revision.

Bina project schedule variance primarily due to geopolitical developments and associated supply chain challenges; recent Middle East conflicts have further impacted supply pricing and execution timelines for Bina.
Brazil FPSO tender took almost 3 years to finalize, delaying project completion to 2031-32 and contributing to the year's impairment.

subsections.label: Outlook
points: Management expects price stability and normalization of the current geopolitical/supply disruption by around July-August, once the war and Strait of Hormuz blockade issues are resolved.
No major stress currently foreseen on the balance sheet, provided crude prices settle; management does not expect debt-to-equity to exceed 1:1 at the group level even with planned capex.
Once major projects are completed, new cash flows are expected to bring debt-to-equity back to normalized levels (0.4-0.5) within a couple of years.
Company declined to provide guidance on indicative GRMs, noting many parameters influence it.
Management stated it cannot comment on potential shift toward periodic/administered price hikes versus daily price revisions, nor on any industry move back to a regulated pricing regime.

Closing outlook: BPCL's integrated operating model and resilient balance sheet position it to navigate the evolving energy landscape; company reiterated confidence in long-term strategy, execution capability and alignment with Atmanirbhar Bharat vision for domestic energy infrastructure.

guidance_ledger.statement: Capex target for FY '26-'27 is INR25,000 crores; may cross INR25,000 crores, maybe INR26,000-27,000 crores if things go smoothly.
Endeavor to take at least 32% retail segment market share over a couple of years.
Company has taken a target of 2 gigawatts in the immediate period for renewables.
Targeting around 6 million to 7 million metric tons of crude the company should have rights on or profit share from, against ~41 MMT refining capacity.
Debt to equity not expected to go up beyond 1:1 at group level even with planned capex; comfortable to maintain at 0.3-0.4 level normally.
Hopeful that by at least July-August, price stability and normality can come back once the war and Strait of Hormuz blockade is removed.
Generally we avoid giving any guidance on what would be the indicative GRMs; many parameters influence it.
First LNG cargo from Mozambique is expected by mid-2028.
Development commissioned; first gas expected 2031-'32, oil will come in 2031.
Proposed to be a 9 million metric ton per annum refinery and petrochemical complex; environmental/technical studies completed, detailed engineering and financial appraisal underway.
Hopeful within approved project cost plus or minus 10%, company will be in a position to complete the Bina project.
Cannot comment on whether there will be periodic price hikes versus daily price revisions or a return to a regulated regime.
FY26 capex guidance: ₹20,000 crore.
Peak capex: FY28 ~₹34,000 crore.
Peak capex: FY29 ~₹35,000 crore.

risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tension in West Asia / Strait of Hormuz disruption
risk_register.note: Driving global and domestic energy supply chain disruption, forex fluctuations, and heightened crude/product price volatility toward year-end; term crude receipt reduced to 45-46% vs 55% planned due to Hormuz constraints.

risk_register.risk: Under-recoveries on deregulated fuels without recovery roadmap
risk_register.note: Management views this as a short-term, not permanent, challenge similar to past episodes (e.g., Russia-Ukraine war); LPG (regulated) may get government support but other products lack clear compensation mechanism.

risk_register.risk: Balance sheet stress from cash flow mismatch if under-recoveries persist
risk_register.note: Company can absorb 1-2 months of mismatch; prolonged continuation without price revision could stress the balance sheet and require burden-sharing among stakeholders.

risk_register.risk: Q1 FY27 seen as challenging period
risk_register.note: Full impact of the war not yet reflected in Q4 FY26 results due to timing differences; Q1 FY27 expected to be tougher.

risk_register.risk: Bina project cost/schedule risk from geopolitical and supply chain disruption
risk_register.note: Schedule progress at 23% vs 32% planned; recent Middle East conflicts impacting supply pricing and execution timelines; ~20-25% of project work yet to be awarded carries residual price risk.
FPSO tender finalization took ~3 years, pushing completion to 2031-32 and triggering INR4,300 crore impairment for the year.

Foreign component of Bina project is limited to INR6,500 crore; even 10% INR depreciation would shift this to INR6,000-7,000 crore, limiting overall impact given most of the project cost is INR-denominated.

risk_register.risk: Elevated crude/LPG freight and premium costs
risk_register.note: World scale freight rates rose from 50-55 pre-war to 600-700 currently; landed crude premium over benchmark currently $10-12/barrel vs Brent plus $4-5 pre-war; LPG spot premiums of $200-300 over Saudi CP when term unavailable.

risk_register.risk: Retail market share loss versus peers
risk_register.note: Management acknowledged a year of relative market share loss compared to other peers, attributing focus to supply chain continuity over aggressive share gains in the current environment.

risk_register.risk: Uncertainty from Aug’25 US tariff measures
INR near historical lows amid US‑India tariff concerns

themes.label: Geopolitical uncertainty
themes.note: West Asia tension and Strait of Hormuz disruption driving price volatility, forex fluctuations and term-to-spot crude shift; Q1 FY27 flagged as challenging.

themes.label: Capex cycle
themes.note: FY26 capex at INR20,400 crore; FY27 capex target raised to INR25,000 crore, potentially INR26,000-27,000 crore, allocated across Bina/petrochemicals, marketing, BPRL and CGD.

themes.label: Inventory management
themes.note: Inventory gains helped refining margins in Q4 amid price volatility; crude inventory maintained at 27 days, product at 24 days.

themes.label: Market discipline
themes.note: Management prioritizes long-term sustainable market share (target 32% retail) over temporary gains, even amid a year of relative share loss versus peers.

themes.label: Renewable energy investment
themes.note: 251 MW installed capacity with 100 MW under execution and 2 GW target; lower 8-9% returns accepted for net-zero balance, primarily used within refineries.

themes.label: Under-recovery and pricing regulation
themes.note: LPG negative buffer at INR12,319 crore; under-recoveries persist on deregulated fuels with no clear recovery roadmap, viewed as short-term challenge by management.

themes.label: Upstream project execution
themes.note: Mozambique progressing at 42% completion with force majeure resolved; Brazil delayed to 2031-32 due to FPSO tender delay, triggering INR4,300 crore impairment.

key_takeaways: We have increased our Russian crude procurement from 25% in Q3 to 31% in Q4, and it continues to increase fill up our supply gaps in the light of the current situation.

During the year, our refineries operated at 116% of utilization with refinery throughput of 41.15 MMT, which is highest ever and distillate yield of 84.54%, reflecting the strength and complexity of our refining portfolio.
Our gross refining margin for the year 2025-'26 stood at USD11.74 per barrel.
During the year, our overall domestic sales volume stood at 54.18 million metric tons at an overall growth of 3.5%, with petrol sales growing by 5.7% and diesel by 1% and ATF is 11.4%.

As of March 2026, the cumulative negative buffer towards LPG compensation stood at INR12,319 crores. This is after accounting for the 5 installments received from Government of India from November 2025 against the announced compensation of INR7,594 crores.

Our gas business continued to deliver strong growth momentum during the year. The annual sales volume stood at 2.29 MMT, registering a growth of 26.5% year-on-year, while the CNG segment recorded sales volume of 248 TMT, reflecting a robust growth of 62.1%.
On an overall basis, we incurred a capex of INR20,400 crores. The capex target for FY '26-'27 is INR25,000 crores.
The revenue from operations stood at INR134,896 crores. The stand-alone profit after tax at INR3,191 crores and the consolidated profit after tax was INR5,625 crores.
While our financials for FY '25-'26 have been strong since the large impact of the war is not fully realized in Q4 due to timing differences. Q1 '26-'27 is going to be a challenging period.
pressing_questions: Now sir, I am absolutely perplexed on this statement, which you've made. Because, sir, I mean, we all are aware about what kind of under recoveries today we are facing across all the products? And sir, I mean, just my question to you, honestly, is more as an investor is that if today, bread prices can move up by INR5 and milk can also go up at the same quantum, what's actually stopping the fuel prices from moving up?

So sir, I mean, what we saw yesterday, I mean, a INR0.90 hike or something. So sir, I mean, why can't we go back to a mechanism or what are the hurdles we are facing from going back to the daily pricing wherein the pass-through is quite simply done on a daily basis, which was much before 2022? So, can we go back to that era again?
So any thoughts on that, sir?
Given the current situation, is it fair to assume that we could see some meaningful price hike at periodic intervals rather than complete move back to daily price revisions?

The company is investing heavily in refinery upgrades, petrochemicals, and renewable energy projects, while managing risks associated with inventory and pricing strategies.

quarters.summary: Pine Labs delivered ~20% YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY2027 (guided FY27 range of 21-23.5%, with Q1 expected at the lower end), with adjusted EBITDA pressured by front-loaded proactive investments in 500 sales people, telecom/network infrastructure, and cloud/AI capabilities; management expects contribution margin to return to the 73-74% range in H2, does not see EBITDA margin going below last year's 23.5%, and reiterates full-year working capital under 15% and ~29-30% full-year tax rate.

key_figures.label: Adjusted EBITDA management would have preferred
Portion of network cost expected to recur

subsections.label: Overall financial performance
points: Management characterized Q1 as another very strong, powerful performance with ~20% YoY growth, versus full-year guidance of 21-23.5% growth, having earlier said Q1 would be at the lower end.
PBT was described as 'quite interesting' at ~Rs.38 Crores; PAT came in close to Rs.20 Crores.
Effective tax rate for the quarter was 46% because tax losses in individual international loss-making entities cannot be absorbed / are not recognized; full-year expected around 29-30%.
India continues to be taxed at 25.1%.

subsections.label: Front-loaded investments impacting EBITDA
points: Adjusted EBITDA came in at ~Rs.126 Crores versus a preferred ~Rs.135-140 Crores; management framed the gap as ~Rs.14 Crores, noting no pricing pressure or adverse market dynamics — these are proactive investments.
Cloud costs rose ~Rs.10-12 Crores on a quarterly basis; ~25-30% expected to recur, the rest treated as one-time.
Company signed a new multi-year contract with one of the leading global cloud providers, giving comfort on pricing so some of these costs should not return.
Cloud costs were previously guided to grow ~6% YoY.

Network costs rose ~Rs.10 Crores; this hits the contribution margin line (not below it); ~50% expected to continue on a recurring basis, driven by petroleum segment deployment (expanded to ~100,000 POS machines) requiring network upgrade and SIM upgrade, plus network upgrades in global markets.

subsections.label: Operating cash flow & working capital
points: Operating cash flow/working capital came in at ~16%; guidance is to keep it under 15% on a full-year basis, with variance across quarters.
Q1 is typically when large payouts happen — employee payments, variable pays, certain capex advances due to supply chain — yet still landed at ~16%.
FY26 demonstrated a tight working capital of ~13% to 15%.
On early settlement (ICB), there is cyclicality because Q1 ramps up after collection intensity in Q3 into Q4; contribution-related changes should not alter the working capital cycle.

subsections.label: Contribution margin economics
points: Management noted no other company at ~72%, 73%, 75% contribution margins, and intends to remain in that range.

Depreciation on terminals has been kept flat over the last six quarters while the business grew, by asking merchants to make upfront payments and buy terminals so inventory stays off Pine Labs' books.

This upfront-payment model solves both the depreciation problem and the merchant attrition problem (merchants who invest early do not switch midway), but brings low-margin revenue into the stream that dilutes contribution margin.

subsections.label: Issuing & Acquiring Platform (IAP)
points: International IAP grew 40%+ while overall growth was 21%; India IAP grew 24%.

Contribution margin in IAP declined because distribution (lower margin, ~30-40% CM) is growing faster than processing (near 100% CM), especially in international markets where distribution is the entry strategy before moving up to processing.
IAP take rate held at a healthy 1.3%; changes in headline take rates are arithmetic, driven by business mix.
In international markets distribution is used as an entry strategy (e.g., Amazon in Singapore for distribution, a large US restaurant chain moving from distribution to full processing).

Product stack is broader than gift cards: gift cards (e.g., a Nykaa gift card for client engagement/working capital), prepaid cards (forex prepaid, general purpose Visa/Master/Rupay prepaid), and credit issuing/acquiring.
Credit processing business (issuing + acquiring) is present in ~20 countries and is now ~Rs.100 Crores of revenue on a full-year basis.
Added ~10 new brands/logos in Q1; if a new gift card program launches in the market, there is an 85-90% chance Pine Labs drives it.

New India segments being pursued: gaming (e.g., Roblox in-app purchases via gift cards), employee benefits, meal card and fuel/expense card (launch by October for tax savings), and direct-to-consumer open-loop prepaid (Bharat Yatra NCMC metro cards ~15,000/month).

Distribution via own platform (Woohoo / Gift Card Marketplace), direct corporate tie-ups, and large marketplaces (CRED, Amazon); listing fees are part of direct cost. Brands now also listed on Zepto and Blinkit for gift card ordering.
EBITDA margin in the IAP/distribution+processing business continues to expand YoY.
Every incremental processing and distribution comes straight to the bottom line below the contribution line, funding long-term growth.
YoY increase in issuing revenues was Rs.56 Crores with a Rs.11 Crores increase in issuing segment contribution, an incremental contribution margin of ~20% in the issuing segment.

subsections.label: DITP (Digital Infrastructure & Transaction Platform)
points: DITP GTV grew only 4% YoY on a full-year basis, largely due to the bill payments business (Setu), which is per-transaction (not ad-valorem) pricing, where one client moved some transactions in-house.
India DITP growth was ~20-25%; across online, flow-based income and issuing side, businesses grew ~20-25% at minimum.

DITP contribution margin declined from 84.4% (prior year Q1) to 81.7% due to a conscious strategic call to move devices off balance sheet — ~25-30% of deployments now have merchants buy the device upfront, bringing low-margin revenue in; also impacted by network capacity investments.
Absolute contribution margin was ~Rs.125 Crores this quarter versus ~Rs.130 Crores last quarter.

Outside India, Pine Labs does not deploy terminals itself (does not do 'DITP' in the terminal-investment sense) — acts as software/tech and processing provider; e.g., deployed 30,000 terminals with GCash in Philippines over 9 months on software and transaction processing basis only.

subsections.label: Affordability / Flow-based services

Flow-based services help brands, banks and financial institutions acquire, convert and engage customers — spanning EMI, offers, and consumer communications at point of purchase.
Flow-based income and transactions continue to rise steadily; implied flow take rate ~28 bps driven by mix between UPI (growing faster) and affordability.
Affordability monetization comes from fees from all stakeholders (merchant, brand, consumer, terminal); no revenue earned when a consumer converts to EMI on their own banking app.
MDR / aggregator income flows into flow-based income and has been increasing; growth ~60-70% given base effect, driven by mid-market, online business and DCC volumes on Pine Labs rails.
Over the next two quarters, management plans to start disclosing more detail on other flow-based revenue streams reaching meaningful levels.
Flow-based income and issuing side have historically grown ~25%+ YoY.

Mid-market merchants increasingly ask for complex integrations where payments become part of their workflow — described as Pine Labs' sweet spot.
Terminal-side business has grown 12-15% YoY historically.
Credit card transactions growing 10-15% in the market; Apple Pay expected to enter before year-end, seen as positive as more diversified payment types strengthen Pine Labs' payment stack.

Online revenues have grown over 3-4 years; online and bill payments have historically grown 50%+ YoY.
Growth hub: a tech platform giving brands/large enterprises insights on store transactions and consumers; revenue becoming fairly interesting on a full-year basis.
