key_takeaways: Came in at about 20% on a year-on-year growth; guided to about 21-23.5% growth on a full year basis with Q1 generally on the lower end.

PAT came in close to Rs.20 Crores; PBT was about Rs.38 Crores; effective tax rate for the quarter was 46% because of unrecognized losses in international entities, with full-year comfortable at about 29-30%.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at ~Rs.126 Crores versus a preferred ~Rs.135-140 Crores, impacted by front-loaded proactive investments: ~Rs.10-12 Crores cloud/infra increase and ~Rs.10 Crores network cost increase; no pricing pressure or adverse market dynamics.
Invested in 500 new sales people over the last six months (full productivity in 6-9-12 months), front-loaded along with telecom/network and cloud capability investments.

Almost 70%+ of all offline POS transactions are on UPI, with average UPI ticket size north of Rs.1,400; DITP contribution margin moved from 84.4% to 81.7% on a conscious call to move devices off balance sheet.

Malaysia is now the single largest installment payments provider (working with ~8-9 banks); services replicated in Singapore and about to launch in Dubai; signed British Airways gift card program and the biggest US organized restaurant chain for processing.
First payments company in India to deliver an end-to-end agentic payment transaction; SignalIQ signed with 6 banks/NBFCs; J&K Bank live on credit on UPI; ~50% of terminals self-healing.
Full-year contribution margin expected to return to the 73-74% range in H2; EBITDA margin not to go below last year's 23.5%; working capital under 15% for the full year.

What was the India GTV growth rate in DITP versus the reported 4% YoY?
For DITP contribution margin dropping from 84.4% to 81.7%, is it a mix shift toward mid-market given pricing power is said to be returning?
What are the levers to accelerate the domestic processing part of the IAP business?

Does the normalization of contribution margin dilute the company's working capital cycle?

subsections.label: Business structure
points: Two large business lines: (1) digital infrastructure and transactions business, and (2) issuing and acquiring side (now almost ~30% of revenues).

Within digital infrastructure and transactions there are three parts: offline and online infrastructure business (operating with large merchants); flow-related transaction services monetized by transaction or value of flow; and Fintech infrastructure for banks/financial institutions and merchants.

Layered model: bottom layer is infrastructure and its distribution (~2 million touch points); middle delivers sector-specific solutions for retailers and banks; third layer brings customers via affordability, loyalty, rewards, cashbacks; newest is data-based monetization / marketing services.

subsections.label: Offline and online infrastructure
points: Present with the top three e-commerce companies and top three quick-commerce companies via payment-gateway-based platform; online business grew almost 60% YoY and is seen as a significant growth area.
Complex loyalty solution developed for the petroleum sector announced with three petroleum companies.
Sub-enterprise merchants (five/six stores) infrastructure business grew almost 30% YoY with about 7% improvement in unit economics.
In select segments, ~7% improvement in unit economics over the last six months.

subsections.label: Flow-based / affordability business
points: Continue to gain market share in affordability; increased the number of brands and signing up more NBFCs to deliver credit at point of purchase (no own NBFC — merchants do not want Pine Labs wedded to one NBFC).
More NBFCs = more lines of credit and more brands where subvention is possible — a strong network play.

Some large banks pulling back subvention offers as certain categories mature (e.g., a large bank reduced offers with a large mobile phone brand over 2-3 years); banks promoting affordability in new areas such as EVs and non-consumer-durable brands.

Where consumer durables uptake is lower, affordability uptake dips; company competes against new lines of credit (e.g., a world-class NBFC delivering point-of-purchase credit for 10 years) by growing store count and credit lines delivered per store to maintain YoY growth.
Multiple flow-based revenue lines: DCC, consumer Fintech partnerships (at least three-four) delivering offers at point of purchase (e.g., 50% off coffee converted to offer-based transaction).

Affordability is broader than lending: post-purchase installment programs, classic personal loans, insurance, trade-in, early buybacks; company not yet playing in new-credit-at-point-of-purchase (PL / consumer durable loans) due to insufficient NBFC coverage.
Affordability done in both offline and online segments; larger online market including non-CDIT.
Non-electronics affordability grew 60% full year (about 40%-45% last quarter) but is less than 5% of the segment relative to electronics — an area to invest in.

subsections.label: Issuing & acquiring / gift cards / IAP
points: Issuing business showed tremendous growth in India and global markets; new use cases from wallets, rewards as an infrastructure play.
RBI streamlining processes/governance of the prepaid (PPI) business, which management appreciates.
Big opportunity in employee benefits — an employee benefits program to be launched over coming weeks/quarters addressing many consumers and corporates.

Distribution and processing are an integrated offering to brands (acquire, retain, grow customers, lifetime value), not two separate businesses; processing flow-through is 95%-98% (tech/AWS/people cost sits below contribution margin); distribution has no incremental cost beyond partner listing-fee shares.

Strong distribution and processing market share in India; international IAP business growing at 44%, started with processing for brands like Woolworths and certain airlines and now building distribution traction internationally.

subsections.label: Data / analytics monetization (SignalIQ)
points: Launched SignalIQ, which looks at consumer data within the account-aggregator framework and delivers analytics-based solutions for better underwriting on behalf of partners.
About eight clients either in pilot or fully contracted for SignalIQ.
Using AI on merchant/consumer data to create new revenue streams delivering consumer insights, a new revenue line growing over the last two years.

subsections.label: Monetization headroom (GDV vs revenue)

Distribution layer is largely linear with nearly all revenues recurring; base layer is largely MSF (rentals); now monetizing GTV through multiple flow and affordability revenue cohorts.

subsections.label: Chip shortage and deployment backlog

Impacted decision making from Middle Eastern banks/FIs by about Rs.15 Crores to Rs.20 Crores; the Rs.20 Crores to Rs.25 Crores of infrastructure revenue management would have liked to see in Q4 was largely infrastructure/deployment related with a small affordability/flow component; has already started coming through from Q1.
Because of the war, suppliers working on 100% advance; company looked at alternate supplies and onboarded supply-chain partners.

subsections.label: Competitive pullback
points: Competition backing off segments because their requirements/business models differ; newcomers pulling out of far-flung OMC / highway / village locations as it is not economically viable without an offline presence.

Some players focus on financial-services monetization (lending) rather than payment-based revenues, so target a different merchant base — an OMC does not need a loan; Pine Labs does no lending business and focuses on merchants who pay for its technology (its 'bread and butter').

Banks and FIs increasingly realize payments is a unique proposition and are calling Pine Labs more; direct-to-merchant strategy paying off; Pine Labs increasingly visible in metros at restaurants, petrol pumps and multi-store merchants.

subsections.label: Long-term stickiness
points: Payments infra business is long-term infrastructure partnerships; for a bank/retailer to replace or displace Pine Labs is a nine-month effort, giving ~nine months' visibility on revenue and low risk of a large revenue miss.

key_takeaways: We came in with about 19% growth on the revenue side. On an adjusted EBITDA side, from somewhere around Rs.357 Crores of adjusted EBITDA, we have now delivered about Rs.559 Crores on adjusted EBITDA. We made almost about 500 basis points improvement on the EBITDA margin side.

Going into FY2027, we have not really given a very specific guidance in terms of EBITDA, but what we have done is we have given out a hard guidance when it comes to revenues. We think we will be able to grow at about 21% to 23.5% on a year-on-year basis as far as revenue is concerned.

We delivered about Rs.113 Crores as far as PAT is concerned. I am glad to say that we delivered almost about Rs.676 Crores of cash flow in Q4 only... on a full year basis where we came in at about Rs.395 Crores of operating cash flow.
On a full year basis, we came in almost close to about $200 billion of payment volume... we are at about 2 million touch points today in the field.

In the online space... we have actually now grown that business almost by 60% on a year-on-year basis. All the three quick-commerce companies, all the three e-commerce companies are today using Pine Labs as a platform.
In our business, almost 89% of all new code, which has been written within Pine Labs over the last two quarters has been completely AI generated.
As far as the issuing business is concerned, our issuing business has shown tremendous growth not just in India but also in global markets... it is now almost about 30% of our revenues.
We have Rs.2700 Crores of cash. We also are organically generating free cash flows... we are quite healthily capitalized for all the growth initiatives we have in mind.
pressing_questions: Given that we are already two months into the quarter, how is 1Q looking and does that make you confident on the 21% to 23%? Will this be something that we will see through every quarter for the four quarters?
Within the digital infra business is it affordability, VAS or the in store subscription piece? Which of these three have actually flowed in 4Q?

This Rs.238 Crores capex, could you break it down between DCPs and what are the other components and how do you expect that to trend? On your contribution margin, this 75%, do you expect this to taper off going ahead?
Can you discuss the trends in terms of the affordability business... because we are seeing a lot of credit card players pull back on offers?
Help us bridge the gap between the 17 and 21 to 23.5 guidance — which revenue pool will see an acceleration? Any color on affordability revenue growth in FY2026 and same-store growth vs expansion?

Historically we have struggled to convert accrual profits into cash profits due to heavy net working capital in affordability... is 30 bps take rate and a shortened working capital cycle from 60-day to 45-day the new normal, and can take rates be maintained at 30 bps?
GDV growth is around 50% whereas revenue growth is around 19%, so is there headroom to increase monetization?

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: Equity indices staged a broad-based recovery over the quarter, navigating geopolitical uncertainty with resilience.
This resilience was equally visible in flows into the domestic asset and wealth management ecosystem, reaffirming conviction in the industry's structural growth story.
India's wealth market remains deeply underpenetrated and represents a significant growth opportunity; for a franchise positioned at the premium end, this is an opportunity to compound leadership.

subsections.label: Net flows commentary
points: Net flows of ~40,000 crores represent 12-15% of the opening ARR AUM base of ~2,40,000 crores.
Net flow split expected to be broadly 70:30 or 75:25 in favour of wealth business.

Asset management net flows were lopsided/negative in the quarter due to one large institutional mandate reducing allocation from ~$550-600 million to ~$175-180 million; broader FII/global allocations to listed equity have been muted over last 6-9 months, though alternates flows have been strong.
Multiple product launches planned over next 6-9 months expected to average out flows between wealth and asset management.
PMS as a structure is challenged structurally versus AIF, mutual fund or SIF vehicles for the same product; strategy remains alive but flows likely to migrate to pooled structures.

subsections.label: Cost-to-income drivers
points: HNI business AUM grew from ~600 crores to ~3,900-4,000 crores last year, and further to ~5,100-5,200 crores this quarter; platform stable, execution digital, run with 65-70 people.
A small set of clients (2-10 crore segment) to be migrated into HNI piece over next 2-3 months.
HNI business expected to not only break even but move into slight profitability this year.
ET Money run-rate loss (excl. exit-related costs) is now ~3-3.5-4 crores per quarter, down from 7 crores last quarter, expected ~6-7 crores this quarter, trending toward breakeven by Q4.
ET Money and HNI improvements expected to reduce cost-to-income by ~100-150 bps combined.
Operating leverage from alternates and wealth management businesses expected to take cost-to-income from 51% to ~49-49.5% by Q4, and ~100-150 bps improvement for the full year.
Core stable UHNI cost-to-income typically ~45%, with 100-200 bps buffer for expansion/new hires; long-term convergence expected toward 44-45% to 46-47% zip code depending on recruitment pace.

Variable vs permanent cost nature: hiring/team costs tied to GBs/JBs (guaranteed/joining bonuses) take 24-30 months cycle (vs 12-18 months) to normalize as new hires rebuild their book; industry equilibrium has not changed dramatically over last 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Retention/yield drivers
points: Retention decline attributed roughly half to carry recognition (largely asset management side, partially wealth) and half to business mix (advisory vs distribution mix, and typically lower TBR in Q1-Q2 vs Q3-Q4).
No reduction in margins seen within any specific business line; decline is purely a mix effect.
Only area of expected continuing headline retention pressure is the pure listed side of asset management business (8-9% of revenue).
AIF-only carry yield estimated at ~4 bps (range 3-5 bps) on ~58,000-60,000 crores alternates AUM, implying ~240 crores annual carry revenue.

subsections.label: Exceptional costs
points: ~12-13 crores exceptional cost this quarter relates to ESOPs tied to the B&K acquisition, not a recurring/constant item.

subsections.label: New SAR grant
points: New SARs (~12 lakh) announced; cost will start accruing only from next quarter once approved and allotted, spread over 4 years (~60 crores total notional impact of ~130-140 crores value).

subsections.label: HNI business
points: HNI proposition scaling well as a natural extension of the UHNI franchise.
Program supported by digital-first, scalable operating model, state-of-the-art client and RM app, and referrals from existing client and RM base.
Expected to break even on direct cost by end of this year as business momentum and productivity build through the year.
Revenue recognition of assets moved to HNI starts with a 12-month lag; trail revenue for assets moved a year ago has just started accruing.
HNI retention will be higher than UHNI distribution retention once mature (85-90 bps vs 71-73 bps for UHNI distribution).

subsections.label: ET Money
points: FY26 was a year of deliberate strategic transformation of ET Money, resetting the business model towards profitability.
Expect business to reach breakeven this year.

subsections.label: Institutional business / B&K integration
points: Institutional equity franchise continues to perform strongly.

Synergies envisaged at acquisition are coming to life: broking income from UHNI clients seeing uplift, and access to 600+ corporate treasuries opening cross-sell into wealth, treasury advisory and lending.

ECM-focused IB capabilities still building out but showing strong early traction; broking mix expected to turn steadily more annuity-like as institutional business scales and UHNI participation rises.

Biggest synergy in immediate short term is on equity brokerage side: combined B&K + UHNI brokerage grown from ~250-260 crores at deal close to ~310-320 crores currently, expected to grow at healthy clip of 15-20% per year for next 2-3 years.
Integration of B&K research into HNW fold expected to make equity brokerage one of the fastest-growing TBR line items.

subsections.label: Asset management business
points: Continues to be a structural growth engine; AUM crossed key milestone of Rs 1 lakh crore.
Strong momentum across alternates platform: private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, renewables, multi-asset, plus listed strategies.
Product engine remains active; continuing to broaden shelf across AIF, PMS, MF platforms including SIFs.

subsections.label: UHNI wallet-share dynamics
points: Number of clients with AUM >Rs 10 crore grown from ~1,800-2,000 (36 months ago) to just above 4,000 currently; these clients typically have only 15-20% wallet share with the firm today.
Growing this base from 4,000-5,000 to 6,000-8,000 clients seen as key to AUM growth via wallet share expansion.
Most clients deal with two or two-and-a-half advisors; ability to be part of that core two (rather than one of four/five) is a key differentiator.
Clients above Rs 250 crores are 70-80% on advisory side; Rs 50-250 crore (or 100-250 crore) segment is roughly 50-50; Rs 10-50 crore segment more skewed toward distribution.

Advisory mix on UHNI incremental flows expected to be ~60-40 advisory-led; advisory clients use the platform ~3x more (trusts, Gift City investments, borrowing, equity brokerage) than distribution clients, so overall retention between advisory and distribution clients is not dramatically different despite lower headline advisory retention.

subsections.label: ECM business build-out
points: Team of 6 people added: 4 on coverage side plus 2 strategic hires on process/compliance side; some serving notice period, some already joined.
Full-strength ECM team expected by October-December, with active pitching for mandates likely from January next year.
Currently a very small business benefiting from existing distribution strength and promoter connects rather than dedicated ECM origination.

subsections.label: Transaction Brokerage Revenue (TBR) composition
points: Large lumpy transactions (e.g., fixed income, private equity syndications) becoming less frequent as co-investment regulation and AIF-PMS vehicles allow long-term money collection for single instruments, converting transaction brokerage income into ARR assets over time.
Only one large lumpy transaction seen in Q4 last year; going forward, ability to have individually large TBR transactions is declining.

Efforts made to keep TBR consistent at Rs 125-150 crores range, targeting modest 10-15% growth over next 2-3 years; overall composition includes equity brokerage (listed), fixed income brokerage, unlisted equity brokerage, real estate/insurance brokerage, and merchant banking income.

TBR expected to stay below 25% of overall revenue mix, but proportion should rise from 15-20% toward ~20% as ARR AUM grows faster than TBR revenue in absolute terms; targeting overall organic growth of 15-20% a year in this bucket.

UHNI wealth management RMs typically break even substantially faster than most other platforms.

subsections.label: UBS collaboration
points: Steady progress across various components of the UBS collaboration; cross-referral programs across NRI, resident, and global mandates showing early traction, expected to convert into meaningful flows over the medium term.
UBS's global distribution expected to open up offshore capital access for alternates and listed strategies during this year.
Onboarding of funds mutually and client referrals began January-March of current year; expect funds launched both ways (UBS launching 360 ONE funds and vice versa) in the coming quarter.
Conservative AUM exchange target of $500-600 million between the two organizations over time, used as the measure of collaboration success rather than immediate cost-to-income/profitability impact.
Confident of seeing money actually change hands over next three months; expect to be close to internal targets by about a year from January-March start.
Both organizations seen as mutually accretive at whatever retention is agreed; exact unit economics/retention terms still to be discovered over next six months as market develops.

subsections.label: 360 ONE Flywheel

subsections.label: Leadership continuity
points: CEO addressed market murmurs about his continuation post any Bain investor step-back; clarified his tenure as CEO is unrelated to his equity shareholding.

Continuation as CEO depends on personal desire/passion (unchanged after 25 years in the business), health (currently 49 years old), and continued alignment of interests; management and CEO remain 85-100% mentally/emotionally invested and >90% financially invested in the business.
No defined timeline (3/5/7/10 years) — approach is continuous, with no factors currently pointing to a change.
CEO noted he has answered the succession question 125 times over 18 years.

key_takeaways: Our total ARR AUM increased by 19% to Rs 3,42,000 crores, with wealth AUM at Rs 2,42,000 crores, a growth of 24.2%, and asset management AUM at Rs 1,00,000 crores, an increase of 8.2%. Overall, AUM rose by 17% to Rs 7.8 lakh crores as on June 30, 2026.

We garnered the ARR net flows of Rs 10,815 crores in this quarter as compared to Rs 8,985 crores in the previous quarter. The wealth business drove the increase contributing strong flows of Rs 13,379 crores as compared to Rs 6,957 crores in Q4.
On the asset management side, even as gross flows remained very strong at approximately Rs 4,000 crores, the net flows were negative due to one large outflow in an institutional mandate.

Q1 FY27 ARR revenues stood at Rs 614 crores, up 20.3% year on year, with ARR revenue now comprising 75% of total revenue from operations. ARR retention was at 74 basis points, with wealth at 71 and asset management at 83 basis points. TBR rose by 37.3% year on year to Rs 208 crores during the quarter. Total revenue increased 20% to Rs 870 crores driven by strong growth across both wealth and asset verticals.

Total cost stood at Rs 446 crores with a cost to income ratio of 51.3% as compared to 53.5% in Q4 FY26. We expect gradual improvement in this metric as the businesses scale up, we drive synergies from strategic initiatives and incoming wealth teams reach full productivity.

We are very happy to report a profit after tax of Rs 330 crores an increase of 14.8%. Tangible ROE stood at 19.4% and we expect this to improve as capital deployed in our lending and asset businesses begin to reflect in earnings.
The program now spans approximately 60+ relationship managers across 12 locations, managing in excess of Rs 5,000 crores of AUM for 800+ clients at ARR retention yield of around 90 basis points.

As business momentum continues and productivity builds through the year, we expect the [HNI] business to break even on direct cost by end of this year. FY26 was a year of deliberate strategic transformation of the ET money business, resetting the business model towards profitability. We expect the business to reach break-even level this year.

AUM has now crossed key milestone of Rs 1 lakh crore with strong momentum across our alternates platform, comprising of private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, renewables, and multi-asset, as well as listed strategies.
pressing_questions: First question is basically on the net flows. I think, you know, we are on the target to achieve that '12 to 15% of opening net flows, but do you think it will be more lopsided towards wealth as AMC is kind of, you know, seeing outflows, specifically in the PMS over the last two to three quarters?

My second question is on the cost-to-income ratio. I think we have this kind of mandate to, you know, go at least 150-200 basis point decline, but this quarter also, it was more than 51%. So, should we expect the remainder of FY27 to have that operating leverage and declining cost-to-income?

An industry question, wherein, you know, we are a significant player in the private credit industry. So just wanted to know, you know, how do you see the future for this segment and how are we kind of positioned to, you know, increase our dominant position further?

Karan, if you can delve some bit on the unit economics of the [UBS] business that you would have in mind, if you kind of reach the $500-600 million asset transfer between the two entities, what kind of revenue potential, or does it operate at a similar cost structure of what we have today?

Over the last couple of months, there have been a lot of murmurs about, you know, when Bain as an investor steps back, you as the CEO might also take a backseat... if you won't mind sharing what, how you think yourself at, from a 3 to 5-year perspective, running 360 ONE, a lot of us would love to hear your thoughts around it.

quarters.summary: Management framed FY26 as a "landmark year" with strong ARR AUM/revenue growth, record PAT, and platform expansion (B&K/360 ONE Capital integration, ET Money, UBS collaboration, HNI Reserve program). For FY27 and beyond, management guided to 12-15% opening AUM net flow growth in Wealth, AUM growth of 20-25%, RM addition of 25-30% per year, and profit growth of 15-25% on the Wealth Management side, while targeting cost-to-income reduction to 45-48% over 2-3 years and quarterly TBR run-rate of ~175-200 crores versus prior guidance of 125-130 crores. ET Money is expected to head toward breakeven in the near term, and the Investment Banking platform under 360 ONE Capital is expected to begin meaningful contribution over the next 12-18 months.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a landmark year for 360 ONE, one in which we have delivered strong financial outcomes, and also meaningfully expanded the platform to complete our flywheel.
Total ARR AUM increased to 311,940 crores, up 26% year-on-year, with Wealth ARR AUM at 2,16,000 crores and Asset Management ARR AUM at 95,000 crores.
FY26 ARR revenue stood at 2,289 crores, up 34.5% year-over-year, and ARR revenue now comprising 75% of total revenue from operations.
We are happy to report the company recorded its highest full-year PAT in FY26 of Rs. 1,225 crores, an increase of 20.7%.
The Board has approved the first interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share.
The integration of B&K is now complete, and the Institutional Equities business has been rebranded as 360 ONE Capital.

On ET Money, FY26 has been a year of strategic transformation on the business model and disciplined execution to drive multiple on-ground changes. With different engines at play, we would expect the business to head towards breakeven in the near term.
As an update to our past communication on tax-related matters, we have received an order today from the tax authorities with an aggregate demand of Rs. 336 crores.

We would love to do better on the mutual fund side, whereas emphasize and ensure that we have our clear leadership position maintained, both on the Wealth Management side as well as on the Alternate side.
We've been blessed to be a large participant in the market and have a large percentage of market share, and we only hope to be able to double our market share over the next 3 to 5 years.
pressing_questions: On the discretionary PMS, growth has been slightly softer than desired — what is the strategy to get back, especially on that segment?

On the UBS bit — in terms of referrals, how has the traction been? Any initial data point? And also, your product on UBS's AMC platform, and then your AMC product on their platform, when can we expect some things on those lines?

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, net flows have come down while retail brokerage has remained more or less steady — is this attrition-led, clients pulling out money, or avoidance of deployment given the volatile situation?

On DPMS, there is a sharp rise in retentions on both Wealth and Asset Management sides — is this new money coming in at higher retentions or older, lower-priced AUM going out, and what is the out-pricing risk given competitive intensity, especially on the Asset Management side?
Some colour on distribution assets where net flow is negative — how much of that negative net flow is from UHNI given HNI would have net positive cash flows?
On the team leader RM count — the count has been broadly flat for the last 3 years despite intense competition; what explains this?

Two key developments during the quarter were the proposed acquisition of gold-loan company Yogloans (entry into secured gold lending) and a USD 400 million oversubscribed international bond issuance strengthening the funding mix.

subsections.label: Book growth drivers

Corporate and SME segments continuing to scale steadily; Corporate segment viewed as having largely maxed out its share, with more incremental growth expected from Retail and SME.
In each business line (Housing, Retail, SME, Corporate, Prime Home Loans) effort is to increase margins even outside the high-margin product mix shift.

Continuing to expand presence beyond captive OEMs while enhancing efficiency through branch and workforce rationalization.

Price gap between new and used vehicles has narrowed after GST rate rationalization.

subsections.label: Microfinance strategy
points: Model is JLG (Joint Liability Group), forming 99.9% of that business; right-to-win seen as operational excellence — correct KYC, income-source evaluation, timely digital collections, paperless processes.
Business seen as having room to scale, but management intends to keep it below 2% of total book for the foreseeable future.

subsections.label: Affordable/Micro Housing strategy
points: Affordable and Micro Housing chosen to target customers within a comfortable credit profile with low delinquency, leveraging cost-of-funds advantage for better ROA.
Micro Housing offers a better yield than Affordable Housing and will be grown faster.

subsections.label: AI strategy
points: AI positioned as a key enabler of the 'Digital First' strategy across the lending lifecycle: onboarding, underwriting, operations, servicing and collections.
Evolution from point solutions to end-to-end, value-creative, transformative AI-led projects across the organization.
AI-powered portfolio monitoring enhances risk surveillance across SME customer portfolios, enabling quicker and more targeted actions.
Number of people added has been small relative to AUM growth, reflecting AI-driven productivity; benefits expected across cost of doing business, faster acquisition, and better cross-sell.

subsections.label: Distribution model
points: Phygital model combines physical branch reach with digital capability, serving 8.8 million customers across existing and underpenetrated markets.

Gold loan branch expansion strategy will focus on building a strong ecosystem in select states (including northern states) before adding more states, once critical mass is achieved in initial states; specific target states not disclosed.

subsections.label: Gold loan (Yogloans) acquisition rationale
points: Combination of Yogloans' domestic expertise and branch network with Tata Capital's brand, technology and risk management capabilities intended to create a compelling platform for secured lending growth.
Transaction structured via combination of capital infusion and purchase of shares from existing shareholders; subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.
RBI approval for the acquisition expected towards the end of the calendar year; organic gold-loan build-out plan will merge with the acquired business once approved.
Acquired team brings experience in the gold loan business; new branches will be added in markets that are growing and behaving well on credit quality.
Competitive positioning in gold loans seen resting on brand trust, cost-of-funds advantage, and strength in technology/operational excellence.

Post regulatory approval, Yogloans will become a Tata Capital subsidiary and will ultimately be consolidated within the Tata Capital brand; no separate branding plan disclosed beyond eventual consolidation.

subsections.label: Funding diversification
points: USD 400 million Reg S bond is the second USD bond issuance and the first following the S&P BBB rating upgrade and equity listing; received broad demand from Asia and EMEA investors including asset managers, insurers, banks and institutional investors.
Foreign borrowings now constitute 11-12.6% of total borrowings (media call cited 11%; earnings call cited 12.6%), reflecting continued diversification of funding mix.

subsections.label: Value unlocking / listing considerations
points: Board discusses potential monetization/listing of Housing Finance business but no decision has been made; company will wait for RBI's placement in the upper layer, which would afford about three years to decide on listing timing, before acting.

subsections.label: Co-lending
points: Company is not a significant player in co-lending market; in early discussions with a few partners who would source loans while Tata Capital retains larger portion of the book; 99% of the book has been built organically.

subsections.label: Macro risks flagged
points: Elevated crude/energy prices from prolonged geopolitical tensions expected to moderate GDP growth from FY26's high base.
Headline CPI crossed the midpoint of RBI's band for the first time since January 2025, led mainly by crude prices; being watched closely alongside monsoon trends and rural demand.
Monsoon and El Niño-related risks being monitored for potential effect on food inflation and rural demand, though no impact seen on portfolio as of the call; hopeful monsoon quantum will improve.
Bank credit growth partly reflects funding substitution as elevated bond yields pushed corporates and NBFCs toward bank borrowings.
MPC held repo rate steady in June, retained neutral stance citing global macro uncertainty; transmission of last year's rate cuts by banks has moderated in recent months.

Temporary liquidity deficit in June from advance tax outflows was addressed via timely RBI interventions; recent measures to encourage foreign currency inflows expected to further support system liquidity.

subsections.label: Segment-specific caution
points: Went conservative in Q1 on Commercial Vehicle and Construction Equipment segments and on MSMEs with high reliance on petro-products, due to concern that full pass-through of fuel prices to end borrowers could hurt profitability of those businesses.
Government has not passed on fuel price increases to end consumers, so these segments have continued to behave well.
No early signs of stress visible in any segment; asset quality across CV and MSME portfolios has shown no material stress despite geopolitical uncertainty.
Elevated fuel costs and macro uncertainties are contributing to a measured, disciplined growth approach in Motor Finance.

subsections.label: Gold loan regulatory considerations
points: RBI revised gold loan guidelines effective this year, creating distinct treatment (LTV, repayment structures) between income-generating and consumption-generating loans; company has planned products in line with these norms.

Company will watch customer leverage levels, collateral offered, and gold price movement trends while growing the gold loan portfolio; views gold loans as a secured asset class with extremely low credit costs.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Management stated Q1 FY27 credit cost of 1% is in line with FY28 guidance and remains well within the guided corridor.
Operating leverage expected to further improve in coming quarters; margins expected to improve due to focus on high margin products.
Company on track to meet FY28 guidance overall (as stated in closing remarks).

ROA improvement to 2.6% expected via two-thirds from margin expansion and one-third from operating cost (OPEX) optimization; any additional benefit from credit cost improvement would be a bonus not factored into guidance.
High-yield/unsecured product contribution expected to make unsecured book growth outpace overall book growth by Q3/Q4 of this financial year.

No policy rate cut/hike benefit has been factored into margin guidance since timing/magnitude of any RBI rate action is uncertain; company will remain neutral to policy rate moves (pass on increases and decreases as they occur).

themes.label: AUM growth momentum
themes.note: Consolidated AUM grew 22% YoY (28% ex-Motor Finance) with strong disbursement growth of 33% YoY, driven by broad-based momentum across Housing, Retail and SME.

themes.label: Asset quality improvement
themes.note: Credit cost declined to 1% from 1.6% YoY, Gross Stage-3 improved to 1.9% from 2.0%, Net NPA down 10bps sequentially, with no early signs of stress in any segment.

themes.label: AI-led operating leverage
themes.note: AI driving 98% digital onboarding, 40% productivity gains, and expected 10-15 bps ROA improvement over next 2 years, with cost-to-income improving 190 bps QoQ to 36.4%.

themes.label: Gold loan diversification (Yogloans)
themes.note: Proposed acquisition of Yogloans marks entry into secured gold lending, targeting 500+ branches and INR4,000-5,000 crore AUM over 3 years, pending RBI approval.

themes.label: Funding diversification
themes.note: USD 400 million bond issuance oversubscribed 4x following S&P BBB upgrade, raising foreign borrowings to 11-12.6% of total borrowings and diversifying the funding mix.

themes.label: Margin/NIM expansion strategy
themes.note: Targeting ~10 bps NIM improvement in FY27 via higher share of high-margin products and better pricing across all businesses, expected to outpace 8-10 bps cost of funds increase.

themes.label: Macro and segment-specific caution
themes.note: Management flagged energy price/geopolitical risks and monsoon/El Niño watchfulness, and went conservative in Q1 on CV, construction equipment and petro-reliant MSME segments, though no material stress has materialized.

key_takeaways: Consolidated AUM stood at INR2.91 lakh crores, up 22% year-on-year and up 5% sequentially; excluding motor finance business, AUM grew by 28% year-on-year.
Credit costs for Quarter 1 FY27 were 1% versus 1.6% for quarter one of FY26, a significant drop.
Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR1,547 crores, up 56% year-on-year and 3% sequentially.
Our Net NPA declined by 10 basis points sequentially to 0.8%. Our ROA stood at 2.3% consolidated including the motor finance business; excluding motor finance, ROA stands at 2.5%.
Tata Capital Housing Finance AUM increased 24% year-on-year to INR89,416 crores; profit after tax for the quarter was up 29% year-on-year to INR532 crores.
Our core focus remains as retail and SME lending which together constitutes 85.4% of our portfolio.
We expanded our distribution network to 1,491 branches across 1,091 locations, serving approximately 8.8 million customers.
Proposed acquisition of Yogloans marks an important step in expanding and diversifying our lending franchise, entering the gold loan segment.
Tata Capital successfully raised USD400 million through an international bond issuance that was oversubscribed four times, strengthening its diversified funding platform.
We had given certain guidance for FY28 and we are on track to meet that guidance going forward.

quarters.summary: Five-Star delivered its best-ever quarterly disbursements (INR1,496 crores, +23% QoQ, +16% YoY) and 4% sequential AUM growth to INR13,722 crores, with management confident of comfortably achieving full-year AUM growth guidance of ~20%, credit cost guidance of 1.7-1.9% (trending to lower end), GNPA falling to sub-3%, and disbursement run-rate of INR6,500-6,800 crores for FY27. Collections and asset quality continued to improve sequentially despite the seasonally soft quarter, opex/cost-to-asset is expected to stay elevated this year (5.75-6%) before operating leverage kicks in from FY28, and management reiterated plans to enter a new product (beyond housing) in the next 3-6 months.

subsections.label: Growth & Collections
points: Quarter panned out in line with expectations, vindicating actions taken to overcome challenges faced.
Historical best disbursement quarter driven by strong traction; at this pace of quarterly growth, full-year growth guidance should be achieved comfortably.
Collections remained robust despite being the seasonally soft quarter.
Current book and 30-plus book both improved sequentially, supported by strong collections.
Slippages remained flat sequentially; credit cost dropped despite seasonally soft quarter.

subsections.label: Cost of Funds & Spreads
points: All-inclusive borrowing cost remained favorable despite not-so-favourable liquidity conditions, helping cost of funds on book decline QoQ.
Spreads remained intact despite yield drop stemming from October 2024 rate cut, showing franchise strength with external stakeholders.
Yield decline of 12 bps was more than compensated by 15 bps drop in average cost of funds, resulting in 3 bps higher spread QoQ.
NIM continues to be flat.
Spread should largely remain flat to current levels for the next few quarters, assuming no policy actions (Chandrasekhar Sridhar Q&A).

subsections.label: Opex / Cost-to-Asset
points: Given competitive intensity, company had to be more competitive on employee compensation; not guiding for strong operating leverage this year.
Whatever operating leverage arises will likely be absorbed by increased expenses; opex will largely stay flat vs last year.
From next year (FY28) onwards, operating leverage should start kicking in; cost-to-asset expected to settle at 5.25-5.5% in steady state vs current ~6%.
Employee cost increase is due to realigning/revising salaries and better incentives at branch level (branch managers, supervisors), not ESOPs.
Overhead cost increase is primarily driven by personnel expenses, not branch expansion, since branch additions this year will follow normal run-rate of 50-60 branches.
Y-o-Y expense growth expected at 20-21%, largely in line with Q1 trend; increments and appraisals already built into Q1.

subsections.label: Yields
points: Large part of asset yield repricing at lower rate is largely over; incremental yield contraction limited going forward.

Q1 average yield less than 22.5%; new loans onboarded at close to 22.5% average (range 21.5%-23%); expect further ~10-15 bps contraction over next couple of quarters, settling around 22.25%, mainly due to NPA interest reversals rather than fresh repricing.
October 2024 200 bps yield reduction was not regulator-driven; it reflected passing back the benefit of borrowing cost falling from 11%+ to 9%+ to customers.
Going forward, lending rates will get adjusted in line with borrowing cost trends (both up and down).

subsections.label: Provisioning & Write-offs
points: Credit cost shown at gross level; recoveries on write-off loans are not netted off against credit cost but shown as other income in top line — divergent from some market practices.
Company does not resort to ARC sale.
Write-offs are technical (for tax benefit and appropriate GNPA positioning); no concerns on recoverability, and recoveries on write-offs continue to be realized.
Company will endeavor to maintain overall ECL coverage of 1.75-1.8% on the book, via a mix of Stage 1/2 coverage build-up or Stage 3 coverage depending on portfolio mix.

subsections.label: Repayment Rate Dynamics
points: Repayment rates rose due to stronger collections (collection efficiency improving from ~96-97% levels).

Policy change: best customers (zero DPD elsewhere) no longer required to fully prepay existing loan before sanction of fresh loan; will instead get a top-up — reduces customer migration to other NBFCs and should help repayment rate normalize to ~27-28% versus current ~30%.
Behavioural loan tenor expected around 4-4.5 years.

Vintage on book (share of 3-5 year loans) rising as loans season; this is distinct from disbursement tenure — nearly 85-90% of loans are disbursed for 7-year tenure; growing disbursement momentum increases share of less-than-1-year book.

subsections.label: Leverage & Debt
points: Absolute debt declined from March levels as company was choosy on borrowing given cost-of-funds focus; adequate lines available to lever up as needed.
Company still holds sizable liquidity (INR1,850 crores) on balance sheet; Q1 tends to be muted for additional borrowing as banks wait for results before setting limits.
Incremental cost of funds guided at 8.5% (not 8.3%) to account for intent to lever up balance sheet, including a pending ADB ECB tranche with hedging cost impact.
Debt-to-equity of 2x will take medium term — likely another 6-8 quarters — given growth trajectory in current and new products and annual net worth accretion of ~INR1,100-1,200 crores PAT.
Leverage will get a kicker even from current product growth, and further boosted with new product additions; endeavor is to maximize shareholder ROE via appropriate capital use.

subsections.label: ROE/ROA Framework
points: Current ROA ~8-8.5% (AUM basis) translates to ~7-7.25% on total assets basis; as leverage increases, ROA compression is expected.
Past guidance was steady-state ROA of ~6-6.5%; at ~3x leverage, ROE could be in 18-20% range — this remains the endeavor.

key_figures.label: Average ticket size on incremental disbursements

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: No dearth of demand in this segment — demand was always there; challenges over last 3-4 quarters led to conscious slowdown in approval rates/disbursements to prioritize asset quality first.

Split of business and collections verticals significantly increased productivity — previously same person managed both business and collections, and stressed accounts negatively impacted disbursement capacity; now dedicated collections team frees business team to focus purely on incremental logins/business.
Strong traction seen in logins and in sanctions converting into MODs, which will convert into disbursements.
Assuming same Q1 disbursement run-rate (~INR1,500 crores) for next 3 quarters plus 10% uplift, projects ~INR6,500-6,800 crores full-year disbursements, comfortably enabling 20% growth guidance.

June monthly disbursement of INR670 crores reflects typical third-month-of-quarter seasonality; company working to minimize inter-month seasonality within quarters; INR600-670 crores expected as new normal monthly run-rate for rest of year.

subsections.label: Ticket Size / Customer Mix Strategy
points: Ticket size increase reflects a combination of inflation and conscious strategic movement to a higher mix.
Target mix: 25% around INR3 lakh ticket size, 50% around INR5 lakh, 25% around INR10 lakh — steps taken are getting reflected in portfolio mix.

Company is not vacating the sub-INR3-lakh/microloan space that other players have exited in the last 12 months — instead becoming stronger in the same space it has operated in for 24 years; only the internal mix is shifting.
Guided mix from last July call: <INR3 lakh ~25%, INR3-5 lakh ~50%, >INR5 lakh ~25% — trend as of June confirms this mix is playing out as planned.
Focus on adding the 'right' customers (good NACH behavior, repayment, flow characteristics) rather than simply smaller-ticket customers.

subsections.label: Competitive Landscape
points: A few other competitors entering the space has required the company to be more competitive on employee compensation.

subsections.label: Asset Quality Stress / Overleverage Monitoring
points: Management sees comfortable collections trends going forward, with collections trending up for the last 7-8 months, indicating intact customer cash flows.
Two watch-items flagged: energy cost increases (which may go up further) and liquidity/regulatory rate decisions.

Rollback stabilization: journey is more about stabilization (holding customers in the same bucket via unique customer collection efficiency) than high rollback, since customers generally cannot pay multiple installments in a month to roll back.

Customer scrub: underwriting cannot fully control future overleveraging, but company has taken measures over last 12 months to withstand any future overleverage crisis; leverage ex-gold loans has trended lower via write-offs and stricter lender guardrails, while gold loans as a category continue to rise.

Gold loan/microfinance small-ticket borrowing is sometimes used by customers to temporarily bridge cash flow dips and repay secured lenders — a seasonal/behavioral phenomenon seen across quarters, not unique to current period.

In the last 6 months, gold loan growth has moderated due to gold price corrections (versus faster growth from rising prices before that), reducing the extent to which rising gold loan values could be masking underlying customer stress.
Microfinance overlap proportion has trended down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% due to stricter guardrails implemented by microfinance companies.

Underlying customer cash flows have remained largely flat rather than showing major improvement, but are viewed as adequate to service secured lenders; behavior (not cash flow) was the primary driver of past stress, linked to write-offs by unsecured lenders.

subsections.label: Steady-State Portfolio Framework
points: Thumb rule for steady state: Stage 1 ~90-91% (current ~87-88%, 1-30 bucket ~3-4%), Stage 2 ~6-7% (31-60 and 61-90 buckets ~3-3.5% each), Stage 3 (NPA) at sub-3%, guided around 2.5% — considered the sustainable business model for short-to-medium term.

subsections.label: Product Diversification
points: Management reiterated intent to diversify into 2-3 products; one new product expected to be launched in the next 3-6 months.
Learning from the recent crisis: being in a single product is risky during stress periods even though depth exists for growth in that single product; Board has emphasized multiproduct strategy.
At the appropriate time, management will explain the specific new product and its rationale to investors.

New product under discussion is distinct from the housing product already launched two quarters ago; housing product was deprioritized while focus remained on getting Micro LAP back to pre-crisis disbursement levels.
Once Micro LAP is fully back on track, focus will shift to scaling the already-launched housing product for similar customer profile, in addition to exploring the new (third) product.
At the point of new product launch, AUM growth guidance would be incremental/additive to the current Micro LAP guidance, not a replacement of it.

subsections.label: Organizational Structure
points: Chairman Lakshmipathy operates on the operational front as MD, supported by JMD/CFO Srikanth, with operational heads/chiefs across all departments — investor presentation includes details of ~20-21 management team members.

Business and collections verticals have been segregated, but business team retains responsibility for collecting on current accounts for a certain vintage — arrears management alone has moved to the dedicated collections team.
No cultural shift or incentive structure changes for the business team; incentives remain tied to both collection percentage on current accounts and growth targets.
Management emphasized Five-Star is not dependent on a few individuals but on its 15,000 employees — 'individuals may come and go, but the institution will go on forever.'
Attrition trends are currently flat; too early to assess impact of compensation realignment, with clearer trends expected in 2-3 quarters.

subsections.label: Flagged Headwinds
points: Energy cost increases, which have gone up and may rise further, flagged as a factor to monitor for customer cash flows.
Regulatory/liquidity environment: uncertainty on regulator's stance on price hikes flagged as a factor to monitor.
Repo rate risk: if there are repo rate increases, this would negatively impact cost of borrowings; current guidance of 10-15 bps further cost-of-borrowing decline assumes no repo rate hikes.
Customer overleverage risk: company cannot control customer-level leverage buildup even with strong underwriting, dependent on lender discipline/guardrails across the industry.
Portfolio in the 61-90 day bucket still carries slippage risk, cautioning against assuming too much write-off benefit this year.
Rating upgrade (carried from prior quarter context) remains contingent on sustained improvement in collections/asset quality trends.

key_figures.label: Further cost of borrowing decline expected

subsections.label: Overall Confidence
points: Management extremely confident of achieving all guidances comfortably in the quarters to come.
Full year growth guidance should be achieved very comfortably given current quarterly growth pace.

Coming quarters (September, December, March) expected to show slippages, credit cost and NPLs all trending down, with credit cost trend likely closer to 1.7% (lower end of guided range) rather than higher end.
New product AUM growth, if launched, would add to (not replace) current guidance.

themes.note: Current book improved to 83.30% from 82.69%, 30-plus book fell to 12.38% from 12.69%, and slippages/credit cost trended down sequentially despite a seasonally soft quarter.

themes.note: Disbursements hit a historical best of INR1,496 crores (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) and AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR13,722 crores, putting 20% full-year growth guidance comfortably in reach.

themes.note: Cost of funds on book fell to 8.80% from 8.95% QoQ; incremental borrowing guided at 8.5% including a pending ADB ECB tranche, with debt-to-equity of 2x targeted in 6-8 quarters.

themes.note: Segregation of business and collections verticals has driven significant productivity gains in logins and disbursements, though business team retains current-account collection responsibility.

themes.label: Ticket size / sweet-spot strategy
themes.note: Company continues to shift mix toward 25% <INR3 lakh, 50% INR3-5 lakh, 25% >INR5 lakh tickets, while explicitly not vacating its traditional micro-ticket space.

key_takeaways: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year.
We ended the quarter with an AUM of INR13,722 crores, which is a sequential growth of 4% for the quarter.

For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we clocked a unique customer collection efficiency of 97.9% versus 98.1% last quarter, with our x-bucket collections coming in at 99.2% versus 99.3% in previous quarter.

Our current book continues to improve and stood at 83.30% as compared to 82.69% as of previous quarter. We also saw a good improvement in our 30-plus book, which reduced to 12.38% as compared to 12.69% in the previous quarter.

Our slippages remained flat at 0.70% compared to the previous quarter. And despite the seasonally soft nature of this quarter, our credit cost dropped sequentially to 1.85% for Q1 financial year '27 from 1.88% for the Q4 financial year '26.

On the borrowing front, our all-inclusive cost was at 8.33% despite not so favourable liquidity conditions. This has also helped bring down our cost of fund on the book from 8.95% for Q4 to 8.80% for the Q1 this year.
During this quarter, one other milestone that we crossed is to achieve 500,000 active loan customers as on 30th June, which is a very significant milestone in the journey of the company.
We ended the quarter with about INR271 crores of PAT. And our net worth as of 30th June stands at about INR7,653 crores.
pressing_questions: Chandrasekhar Sridhar asked whether the rise in gold loans could be masking underlying stress not actually improving, given the overlap of Five-Star customers with gold loan and MFI borrowers.
Rajiv Mehta questioned whether the credit cost guidance of 1.7-1.8% implies management is planning to build back coverage on Stage 1 and Stage 2, given fresh flow rates have normalized significantly.
Kunal Shah asked where current book (~99.2% collection efficiency) and 30-plus/current book metrics would settle 2-3 years down the line as the portfolio matures and underwriting improves.
Divyansh Gupta asked for the overall (not just unique customer) collection efficiency numbers for the current and prior quarter — management deferred this to the IR team.
Chirag Fialoke asked for the 60-90 day bucket percentage for the quarter — management deferred this to the IR team.

quarters.summary: Management stated the worst of the asset-quality stress (from MFI overlap in small-ticket secured lending) is behind Five-Star, with collection efficiency back to normal levels and disbursements re-accelerating in Q4FY26. The company guided to ~20% AUM growth for FY27 (18-20% range, ~INR16,000cr AUM by FY27 end), disbursements of INR6,200-7,000cr, steady-state credit cost of 1.5-1.6%, ROA of 8.25-8.5% for FY27 (steady-state 8-8.25%), spreads of ~13.5%, and opex/AUM of 7-7.25%, with cost of funds expected to stay largely flat versus FY26 due to geopolitical/macro uncertainty.

key_figures.label: Return on average AUM (alt figure cited by CFO)
Cost of funds excluding ADB borrowings

subsections.label: Q4 PAT drivers
points: PAT for the quarter was 3% lower sequentially on account of higher personal expense (build-out of collections vertical plus typical Q4 incentives/schemes to spur collections and growth), while full-year PAT still grew 2% despite the challenging year.

Personal expense increase described as not a one-off but a typical Q4 phenomenon, combined with the collections vertical build-out; growth being slightly lower this year made personal costs look higher on the margin.

subsections.label: Cost of funds / borrowing
points: ADB $100mn line drawn $50mn in Q4, with another $50mn available to draw anytime in FY27; all-inclusive cost slightly higher than previous quarter primarily due to higher hedging cost on the ADB transaction.
Excluding ADB borrowings, overall cost for the quarter would be ~8.25-8.3%.
Management does not expect much benefit from cost of funds in FY27 given macroeconomic/geopolitical uncertainty creating uncertainty in the borrowing space; will keep pushing banks for finer rates.

Rating upgrade unlikely at least till second half of the year until benefits are shown; average borrowing rates expected to remain closer to 8.5% levels, implying another 30-40 bps of cost still to flow into the book over the next two to three years.
In April, no borrowing was done given strong liquidity position; better clarity expected over next couple of months and next earnings call.

subsections.label: Provision coverage / Stage-2
points: Stage-2 proportion (61-90 day bucket) improved, dropping from 5.1% to 4.8%, causing a small drop in Stage-2 provision coverage; company tracks overall provision coverage as the key confidence metric on balance sheet/asset quality.
RBI has prescribed a minimum floor (5%) on Stage-2 for banks; management does not expect this framework to apply to NBFCs soon since ECL framework for banks itself starts only from April 1, 2027.

subsections.label: Spread/Yield dynamics
points: Despite dropping yields by 2% about 1.5 years back, spreads remained healthy; full-year spread drop was only 40 bps despite incremental disbursement cost increase of ~200 bps, due to favorable cost of funds.

Incremental lending yield is ~22.5%; factoring delinquencies, book yield should be closer to 22-22.25%; Q4 book yield was ~22.6%; further impact of ~30-40 bps expected over the next three to four quarters as older higher-yield loans roll off.

Management does not see material yield compression from shifting focus toward higher ticket customers (closer to 5 lakh vs 3 lakh) as segment is not very price-sensitive and yields have been similar across ticket sizes over the last 12 months.

No plan to revise pricing either upwards or downwards at this point despite elevated steady-state credit cost guidance; company already dropped pricing by 200 bps ~1.5 years back and is at the lower end of segment pricing range.

subsections.label: Personnel/Management continuity
points: A senior management exit occurred during the year but had no impact on performance; company emphasizes team depth at management and branch levels, not dependent on any few individuals.

subsections.label: Collection trend / demand recovery
points: Collection efficiency across all buckets showing excellent improvement, returning to robust historical levels; reflects strength in credit underwriting and collection infrastructure.
Current bucket proportion improved for the first time after quarters of continued drop, moving up ~1% from Q3 to Q4.
For last six months, a good upward trend has been seen in collections; NPA expected to start slowing down from next quarter onwards as forward flow from current and x-customer buckets reduces.

April trending in line with a typical seasonally weak month; no material deterioration or improvement expected but collections holding up well across buckets; company does not expect material impact from geopolitical scenario (West Asia conflict) on customer segment, with exposure to small eateries/NRI remittances sub-1% of portfolio and no alarm signals in repayments.

subsections.label: Digital vs cash collections
points: Intent is to move digital collections closer to 90%, though some level of cash collection will always remain given borrower profile.

key_figures.label: AUM in INR3-5 lakh ticket band

subsections.label: Ticket size / product mix strategy
points: Company operating in a 'sweet spot' of INR3-5 lakh ticket size, viewed as the segment with highest growth potential and highest barriers to entry for competitors.

Prior guidance (three quarters back) was to slow down below INR3 lakh (where pain was seen) and focus a bit more on above INR5 lakh; no major structural shift to bigger ticket sizes has occurred - over 50% of AUM remains in the INR3-5 lakh band.

Micro-LAP product (sweet spot INR3-5 lakh) being pushed back to its original growth trajectory due to good yields, returns and runway; affordable housing product being introduced in some locations with a target sweet spot of INR7-8 lakh; one more product may be added in the next two years.

subsections.label: Geographic growth composition
points: Large chunk of FY26 AUM growth came from non-South markets (Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, UP) as branches were newly put in these states; AP notably weaker this year.
South (~85%+ of AUM) is where the over-leverage problem started; growth was muted there for first two quarters (June, September) as focus shifted to collections.

For FY27, growth of South markets (Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana, and to some extent Karnataka) expected to predominantly drive the anticipated 20%+ growth as collections stabilize (Karnataka x-bucket collections at 99% last quarter).

subsections.label: Branch expansion strategy
points: Endeavour is to keep opening new branches to stay close to customer vicinity (25-30 km catchment) where competition is lower and ground-level understanding of customers is better - considered an important lever for growth.
95% of the 90 new branches opened last year have already broken even, indicating infrastructure is in place to support doubling growth versus last year.

For FY27, plan is to open a comparatively smaller number of 60-75 branches versus 90-96 last year, as the split branch mechanism and new branch infrastructure built over the last three years in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, AP has provided a strong foundation; if newer states (Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat, UP, Chhattisgarh) show promise, branch counts there will be increased.
Branches will typically break-even or become profitable over a nine to 12 month period.

key_figures.label: AUM share shown from certain new geography (city-level split)

subsections.label: Maharashtra / Tier1-2 expansion
points: Uptick in city-level AUM split (from ~1% to 2%) driven by new branch openings in Maharashtra (Nashik, Pune, Aurangabad) classified as Tier 1/2 cities, not a change in sourcing strategy - branch network in Maharashtra being scaled from ~40 to 70-80 branches as the state looks promising.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning vs fintech
points: Management does not view fintechs as competitors because fintech ticket sizes (INR25,000-50,000, below INR1 lakh) and tenures (6-12 months) differ fundamentally from Five-Star's average ticket size of ~INR4 lakh and tenures of up to 7 years.

Five-Star's loans are for business construction purposes (business improvement, starting a business, home renovation) vs. fintech's working-capital-like use; fintech may compete more with gold loan providers of similar ticket size/tenure.

On digital footprint concern (customers gaining banking history from digital payments potentially attracting fintech lenders), management acknowledged that digital footprints are becoming inevitable everywhere, but reiterated ticket size and tenure differences insulate Five-Star's customer base from fintech disintermediation.

subsections.label: Underwriting methodology
points: Proprietary underwriting based on evaluation of character, cash flows, and collateral, perfected over 20 years of operating in this segment; process, credit bureau footprint review, and underwriting is the same regardless of ticket size (INR3-5 lakh vs INR5-10 lakh); sourcing channels are also the same across ticket sizes.
Management offered to take interested analysts through detailed underwriting process, turnaround times, etc. in offline discussions rather than during the earnings call.

subsections.label: Organizational restructuring
points: Business and collections verticals fully separated into distinct teams effective April 1, 2026; business team now focuses on new business origination while collection team focuses on stabilizing DPDs across all customers.
Restructuring undertaken in response to the over-leveraging cycle experienced for the first time in the company's ~20-year history, requiring reorganization of the team structure.

subsections.label: Asset quality stress
points: Asset quality headwinds faced by MFIs and unsecured loan lenders over the last couple of years crept into secured loan lenders' portfolios too, especially those providing small ticket loans, due to higher MFI overlap, resulting in increased DPDs and NPA for Five-Star during FY26.
Management maintains actions taken over recent quarters have addressed these challenges and the worst is behind the company.

subsections.label: Macroeconomic/geopolitical risk
points: Geopolitical scenario (West Asia conflict) flagged as a monitorable; management has not seen material impact so far, portfolio exposure to potentially affected segments (small eateries, NRI remittances) is sub-1% with no alarm signals in repayments, but will continue to monitor.
Geopolitical/macro challenges are creating some uncertainty in the borrowing/liquidity space, which is a reason cost of funds is not expected to improve materially in FY27.

subsections.label: Sector over-leveraging
points: Permanent over-leveraging in the microfinance sector flagged in prior quarter's commentary; discussed as an ongoing sector dynamic being closely monitored, addressed via organizational restructuring and slower growth in South markets during first half of FY26.

subsections.label: Personnel risk
points: Senior management exit during the year created an overhang, though management states it had no impact on performance given team depth.

subsections.label: Regulatory (ECL/Stage-2 coverage) risk
points: RBI has prescribed a minimum floor (5%) on Stage-2 coverage for banks; company's Stage-2 coverage is currently lower than this prescription, but management does not expect this framework to extend to NBFCs soon since the ECL framework for banks itself starts only April 1, 2027.

subsections.label: Growth outlook trajectory
points: Company is 'geared up' for AUM growth of ~20% for FY27, and will 'slowly move upwards' thereafter; for at least the next two to three years, growth of around 20% is targeted (conservative range 18-20%), with 20% not being viewed as the ceiling - possible upside if asset quality and credit cost trends remain favorable.

Even growing at 20% by end of FY27, AUM would be only around INR16,000 crores, reflecting a relatively low base versus historical ~INR5,000-7,000 crore AUM base when growth was 30%+; management does not want to over-commit beyond 20% despite low base, given the year is coming off 10-11% growth (effectively doubling growth rate).

subsections.label: Credit cost normalization
points: Credit cost guidance of 1.7-1.75% of average AUM for FY27, an improvement from Q4FY26 actual of 1.88%; if buckets trend better through the year, actual could beat guidance.

Steady-state credit cost guidance of 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30, up from earlier historical guidance framework of 0.8-1% (on total assets basis, equivalent to ~1.3-1.35% on AUM basis); increase reflects revised understanding of the environment/customer segment, need for consistency in credit cost build-up amid macro volatility, and balancing growth with credit cost rather than under-provisioning and pressuring field force.

subsections.label: Disbursement outlook
points: FY27 disbursement targeted at ~INR6,200-7,000 crores (varying figures cited: 6,200-6,400cr and 6,500-7,000cr) to support 20% AUM growth; back-of-envelope calc: FY25 disbursements of ~INR5,000cr (~INR425-450cr/month), a 15% increase would give ~INR6,000cr, another 15% would give ~INR7,000cr for FY27.

Company consciously pulled back disbursements this year amid the credit cycle; ability to grow disbursements 20% off a low base is viewed as not a challenge, with strong lead indicators already visible; Q1FY27 targeted to show strong disbursements despite being a seasonally weak quarter historically.
